In this paper, we explore the application of autoencoders for anomaly-based NIDS, focusing on various types of regularization techniques to enhance detection performance. We compare the performance of three types of autoencoders—vanilla, sparse and denoising—using the benchmark NSL_KDD dataset by evaluating different performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score. We find that the vanilla and sparse autoencoders are suitable for the dataset.

articleTitle: Sucrose Concentration Estimation by Using HSV Color Space Analysis with Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a novel technique to determine the concentration of sucrose by using Benedict’s chemical test and digital image processing. A series of sucrose samples are prepared by mixing with distilled water, covering a range of concentrations from 0% to 50% w/v molar concentration. The images are acquired by using a camera module interfaced with a Raspberry Pi single-board computer. The images are analyzed by using HSV color space. The experimental results demonstrate strong correlations between the color component values and the molar concentrations of the liquid samples. The unique features of the method include its portability, rapid analysis, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for scenarios outside the laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimizer, Ant Colony Optimization, and Quantum-Based Optimization for Document Retrieval: A Comparative Analysis with FLICM and FDMO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The relevancy and accuracy of document retrieval systems are essential for information retrieval tasks, particularly in large-scale and high-dimensional datasets. This study explores the integration of Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Quantum-based optimization into a Fuzzy Local Information C-Means (FLICM) clustering framework for enhancing deep learning-based document retrieval systems. By correlating with recent advancements in Fractional Dwarf Mongoose Optimization (FDMO) for document retrieval, we investigate how these alternative optimizers affect system performance in terms of precision, recall, and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Distinctive Approach to Recognize Vocal Sentiment Using Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Within affective computing, vocal sentiment detection is a new field focusing on speech-based interpretation of human emotions. This work explores cutting-edge expert systems and audio processing techniques to increase the precision and consistency of sentiment detection from voice inputs. This paper examines a deep learning technique for audio file-based emotion identification is presented. In particular, characteristics from these audio files are extracted using a convolutional neural network (CNN) model, which then categorizes the data into 14 different emotions. Over 4,000 audio samples from four distinct sources—TESS, RAVDESS, SAVEE, and CREMA—are used to train the model. This approach improves emotion recognition accuracy by capturing strong and unique elements from audio sources. Experiments on publicly accessible datasets show that the model performs remarkably well recognizing various emotions, including neutrality, happiness, sorrow, and rage. The study also addresses difficulties with speaker variability in vocal emotion identification and cross-cultural variances. The results show significant gains over current techniques, highlighting the approach’s potential for use in emergency contact centres, customer service, security, lie detection, human-computer interaction, and mental health monitoring. The study proposes possible applications to other domains, including language detection and natural language generation (NLG). It lays the groundwork for future research in emotion detection and analysis. The findings of this research hold great promise for developing increasingly complex and human-like interactions between humans and technology.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of EEG Signals Using PSD, FFT and Wavelet Transform Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The study of the human brain heavily relies on electroencephalography (EEG) in today’s world, providing crucial insights into its functioning. Despite its importance, the classification of EEG signals poses a significant challenge due to their complex and dynamic nature. This paper aims to improve the accuracy of classifying EEG signals related to motor imagery (MI) by utilizing robust techniques such as power spectral density (PSD), fast fourier transforms (FFT), and wavelet transforms (WT). These methods, widely recognized and utilized in both academic and industrial settings, are combined with machine learning algorithms including K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Random Forest Algorithm (RFA) to enhance the classification accuracy. This holistic approach aims to address the aforementioned challenges. The goal is to help advance the classification of EEG signals, which will in turn make it easier to explore and understand the dynamics of the brain.

articleTitle: Secure Federated Learning for Gate-Level IP Hardware Trojan Detection Using Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The globalization of pre-silicon to post-silicon transformations in smart circuits through third-party EDA toolchains introduce security challenges, particularly the risk of hardware Trojans (HT). Most existing HT detection methods rely on binary classification models to detect the presence of HTs in pre-silicon Intellectual Property (IP). This paper presents a novel approach to Design-for-Hardware-Trust (Dfht), leveraging machine learning (ML) to predict HT presence with enhanced accuracy. We introduce a federated learning framework using homomorphic encryption to ensure data privacy and security, training HT detection models on decentralized gate-level IP datasets. Compared to the existing untrusted training infrastructure, sensitive information associated with the HT dataset remains unexposed to the proposed federated cloud server. The Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied for data preprocessing to address class imbalance. Our federated-learning-enabled Dfht approach improves IP quality, testability, and security, effectively countering ML-activated hardware back-doors. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in maintaining HT-free designs.

articleTitle: Crop Disease Categorizations Using Optimized Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Detecting crop diseases is essential for agriculture to help farmers for better use of resources and enhances crop yields. propose study use a large dataset of commonly grown crops like cassava, maize, and tomato to test the diseases. Various approaches including machine learning(ML) and deep learning(DL) are being used to identify the disease in crops. The presented study uses convolutional neural network (CNN) based models Inception V3 and EfficientNet to identify diseases in crops. The proposed approach achieves a high accuracy of 97%, demonstrates how artificial intelligence (AI) can improve farming practices through precise crop monitoring and disease management. The findings show that deep learning models, especially CNNs, are highly effective for large-scale crop disease detection and can be used in agricultural applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Heterostructure Vertical HEMTs for Drain Current Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This research project aims to explore how different combinations of heterostructure materials impact the drain current of Vertical HEMTs through simulation software. Improving the performance of electronic devices requires optimizing the drain current in Vertical High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs). This project uses TCAD simulation software to examine how different heterostructure material combinations affect the drain current of Vertical HEMTs. The paper investigates three distinct material combinations: InAlN/GaN, GaN /AlGaN, and InAlN /InGaN. The objective is to determine which combination of materials produces the most considerable drain current by examining and contrasting the drain current values for every heterostructure. The results are anticipated to shed light on the best material combinations for improving Vertical HEMT performance, which could lead to higher-performing and more efficient electronic devices.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Time and Frequency Domain Approaches in Single Channel Foreground Speech Enhancement using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Speech enhancement plays a crucial role in a large number of applications, by aiming to improve the intelligibility and quality of speech signals degraded due to the presence of noise. This paper investigates the performance of deep learning inspired architectures with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for speech enhancement using two different input representations: time series and log-Mel spectrograms of data. Using a suboptimal dataset with limited size, limited training epochs, and constrained hardware, we evaluate the efficacy of these representations under the influence of some random noises. The performances of both models developed accordingly were evaluated on same the test set. The model using time series data as input demonstrated better performance in capturing local patterns and effectively reducing stationary noise, while the one using log-mel spectrogram as input, excelled in modeling the temporal dynamics of the speech signal and therefore reduced the non-stationary noise in the data.

articleTitle: Lead-Free Cs3Sb2I9 Perovskite: Advancing Solar Technology Through Enhanced Efficiency and Environmental Responsibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Thin film perovskite based solar cells (PSCs) outshined over silicon based solar cells with their outstanding photovoltaic (PV) performance. The noticeable features of PSCs are their extended diffusion length, carrier life time and affordability. Moreover, its capability to modulate bandgap is exceptional attraction, allows wide range of wavelengths to get absorbed by solar cells. Hybrid (organic-inorganic) perovskite delivered significant rise in power conversion efficiency (PCE). However, drawback of this material is its limited thermal stability. To deal with this issue, focus of researchers is shifted towards all-inorganic halide (AIH) perovskite materials. As per previous published work, AIH perovskites exhibited high thermal stability against change in temperature/humidity. However, presence of lead (Pb) in AIH perovskite compounds is hazardous to environment as well to living beings. This study proposed a AIH perovskite material Cs3Sb2I9, free of lead, deployed as an active layer in solar cell design. The proposed Cs3Sb2I9 based AIH-PSC, is executed in SCAPS-1D simulator. In this study, impact of acceptor doping/ interface defect density of Spiro-OMeTAD/Cs3Sb2I9-Spiro-OMeTAD is analysed on PV performance of AIH-PSC, for the range 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> -10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> (cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>)/ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> - 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> (cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>) respectively. This work encourages many researchers to work on lead free perovskites.

articleTitle: IoT based dual health monitoring device for liquid infusion and urine level measurement of urine bag
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Advanced healthcare monitoring devices that improve patient care through real-time data collecting, remote monitoring, and individualized therapy have been developed as a result of the integration of IoT technology in the healthcare industry. Vital indications including heart rate, blood pressure, glucose levels, and oxygen saturation may be continuously monitored thanks to these IoT-enabled gadgets, which include wearable sensors, smart implants, and remote monitoring systems. These devices assist in the early detection of potential health issues, enabling timely intervention. They help reduce hospital readmission rates by monitoring patients remotely. Additionally, they enhance chronic disease management by transmitting real-time data to healthcare specialists. Furthermore, by providing feedback and reminders, IoT-based healthcare devices encourage patient participation and adherence to treatment programs. Despite the many advantages, IoT technology's role in healthcare monitoring is about to change patient outcomes as it develops. The progress in technology over the years has made it possible to use smaller devices, such as smartwatches mobiles, for health monitoring and disease detection.

articleTitle: Automatic Evaluation of Descriptive Answer using Optimized Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: As everything in the modern world is automated, examination processes also need to be automated. The Automatic Evaluation system is already established for objective questions, where students can select any choice as the answer and mark it. Since the answer is simple to record and the system evaluates and assigns a grade in an effective manner, the automatic evaluations of this are similarly quite simple. However, descriptive answers are required in order to fully comprehend the student's depth of knowledge, where students can write about their in-depth understanding of the solutions. The manual evaluation of objective type of answers is also very simple because the answer is a single word and the evaluator easily correct the papers and put the marks. Descriptive answer evaluation requires more time and requires additional staff members. Sometimes students will write multiple answers to the same question depending on how students desire to express themselves, and the human evaluators may have fluctuating emotions when assessing the papers, which leads to erroneous evaluations of descriptive answers. In order to address this, we have created a model that automatically evaluates answers that are descriptive in nature and assigns a score between 0 to 10. For this motive, a model is created that accurately assesses students' exam performance through the use of natural language processing and an inventive artificial neural network technique. Similar to a human evaluator, this model is designed for an assessment system and produces results that are more accurate and consistent. When this model is compared to the evaluation scores of human evaluators, it produces results with the best accuracy and that are extremely similar to the scores provided by human educators.

articleTitle: Hourly Trend Analysis of Spatio-temporal Precipitation Extremes Using TRMM and GPM Satellite Data on ETCCDI Indices for the Indian Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: India relies heavily on rainfall for agriculture, water management, and climate planning. Satellite missions like the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) provide global rainfall data, but they haven’t been fully used for studying daily or hourly rainfall in India. This research looks at how daily data from these satellites can help analyze rainfall patterns over time. It uses methods like the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator, compatible with handling satellite data. The study analyzes each hour starting from the 00th to the 21st (00th, 03rd, 06th, 09th, 12th, 15th, 18th, 21st), i.e., daily data split into 3-hour intervals to infer insights into diurnal changes within precipitation patterns. Moreover, through this process, the recent shift of extreme rainfall activities from the Bay of Bengal towards the Arabian Sea is also addressed, and a call for action is made through which the government and meteorological organizations can draw meaningful conclusions for early future calamity prediction.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Alzheimer’s Disease Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Alzheimer’s is one of the progressively debilitating conditions, and it currently affects millions of people worldwide with no definitive medication for treatment. Understanding the nature of this disease is very important and stands to achieve early intervention and management. The development of models to recognize individuals having Alzheimer’s based on neuroimaging data, particularly MRI scans, has thus become accessible through recently advanced machine learning and deep learning algorithms. This paper does a comparison of some of the leading algorithms. Models used for research in this study are Support Vector Machines, Convolutional Neural Networks, 3D Convolutional Neural Networks, and hybrid pre-trained models. There’s model differentiation which resulted in pointing out the gap in the system and weaknesses of each approach. Apart from this, the discovery of the Explainable AI (XAI) concept regarding insight in the predictions of the algorithms has also been emphasized recently. As a result, XAI can improve the interpretability of AI systems. With this perspective, the degree of insight could lead toward better outcomes as far as diagnosis and responses in clinical environments are concerned. Given the importance of the paper, it will suffice to contribute to further refinements of diagnostic methodologies for AD and inform future studies on the subject.

articleTitle: Efficient net-based deep learning: A deep-fake image detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: With the substantial volume of social media data generated daily and the concurrent emergence of powerful multimedia modification techniques, detecting manipulations in photographs and videos has become an important task. This study examines the strength of a deep learning-based efficient net model for detecting manipulation in multimedia images. This study examines the publicly accessible benchmark dataset DFDC to prove its efficiency. We also highlighted the real-world challenges and emerging trends to combat deep-fakes. The research experiment resulted in and confirmed the efficiency of Efficient-Net as it performed well in both the training and testing stages, exhibiting more accuracy and reduced loss. The test accuracy varies between 50 and 95, with epochs spanning from 0 to 10.

articleTitle: Antenna and Antenna Array for 5G n79 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The study represents the performance and designed evaluation of a microstrip patch antenna operating 5G, n79 frequency band i.e.; 4.7GHz, investigated in single and four patched configurations for advanced wireless applications. The antennas are being made on an FR4 (lossy) substrate. The single patch antenna showed a return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) of -48.8327 dB at 4.7014 GHz, indicating good impedance matching. Furthermore, for a four-patch array, the patches are placed in a single line, yielding return losses of -53.3949dB (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>), - 51.878dB (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>), -51.8514dB (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</inf>) and - 51.9272dB (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</inf>) for the selected 5G frequency. The results indicate that both the single antenna and array configuration retain distinguished and wonderful impedance matching and high gain provide the suitable implementation at selected 5G frequency. Such proposed antenna and antenna array offer good performance in lens type arrangement or configuration to achieve the effective beam-forming.

articleTitle: A Weighted Ensemble Approach for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Using CNN and VGG16*
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Detection and classification of brain tumors are essential tasks in medical imaging, focused on enhancing diagnostic accuracy and facilitating early intervention. This study presents a novel weighted ensemble method that integrates the predictive capabilities of a traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a pre-trained VGG16 model for effective brain tumor classification. The dataset employed comprises MRI images categorized as 'tumor' or 'no tumor.' Both models were trained on the data, achieving notable results individually, with the CNN attaining an accuracy of 88% and VGG16 reaching 84%. To enhance performance, we utilized a weighted ensemble strategy, allocating a greater weight to the custom CNN due to its superior performance. The weighted ensemble method demonstrated superior classification performance, achieving an accuracy of 92%, precision of 88%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 93%. The proposed ensemble surpassed individual models and a stacking ensemble in critical metrics, notably in recall, achieving a perfect score and ensuring the accurate identification of all positive cases. The results demonstrate the efficacy of weighted ensemble methods in improving brain tumor detection, presenting a valuable tool for clinical diagnostics characterized by enhanced reliability and robustness.

articleTitle: Four Port Square Shaped Spiral MIMO Antenna at Multiple Frequencies in C Band & X Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Next-generation wireless communication systems increasingly rely on Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) techniques to achieve high data transmission rates. This paper presents a four-port spiral MIMO antenna, designed to operate across multiple frequencies in the C and X bands for wireless communication. The antenna system, which features four radiating elements on a cost-effective FR4 substrate with a thickness of 1.5 mm, operates at frequencies of 5.3 GHz, 5.8 GHz, 6.9 GHz, 7.4 GHz, 10.9 GHz, and 11.6 GHz. The design and simulations were performed using CST software. The proposed antenna has dimensions of 28 mm x 28 mm x 1.5 mm and demonstrates strong performance with isolation below -15 dB, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) under 0.01, nearly 10 dB Diversity Gain (DG), and a gain exceeding 5.5 dB across all specified frequencies. Performance of this antenna is compared with that of similar types of antennas found in recently published papers.

articleTitle: Speech Detection and Comparison using Different Feature Extraction Method for Correct Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Mental status through physical appearance identification is not possible as it does not give complete status of any human. Using voice and considering quality extraction of talked it is quite easy to predict the mental behavior and internal variation that will help the doctor related with medical treatment that support them to give proper treatment to person. Hindi is the natural language of India and large community of population talk and speaks this language to exchange and communicate. Various inputs like specific feature, images and vital report of serious person and it is one of the important facts sources for deep training or gaining systems. In this research paper we try to identify the speech signal under different scenario like gun noise, car noise etc. following different feature extraction approaches and compare it for its proper verification. This verification may help to enhance the quality of speech in different adverse scenario and make the speech detection easy. Here, the comparison has been done with various feature extraction method and the results reflects that MFCC has good efficiency of 95% and with a low error rate of 2% compared to other approach. For analysis Hindi voice sample were used for the experimental analysis for 50 samples.

articleTitle: An Improved Image Steganography Method for Domestic Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Domestic Internet of Things (DioT) environment of a household requires prompt considerations in order to develop proper protection mechanisms for the transfer of sensitive information between linked devices. This created the need for this research work to put forward an improved image steganography technique for DIoT which employs AES encryption to encrypt the cover image and Least Significant Bit (LSB) for the insertion of the secret information table. This paper explains the design and implementation of the proposed method with clear indication of the improvement in security while maintaining system performance for data transfer. Therefore, the results of the evaluation in this article demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid solution for strengthening the confidentiality and integrity of data exchanged within the complex environment of domestic IoT.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sign Language and Audio Conversion Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The appearance of audio conversion and the appearance of gesture language have greatly advanced communication technologies, especially for hearing impairment and blind. These double -purpose technologies promote communication between these groups, provide opportunities for expression and speech behind. The technology uses advanced artificial intelligence algorithms to provide real-time speech and sign language translation to improve accessibility and inclusivity. It is essential to protect data privacy, maintain the accuracy of AI models to avoid misinterpretations, and address ergonomic issues associated with long-term use. Technology converts audio entry into a gestic signal that can be seen by avatars using computer vision and natural language processing. There is a depth learning model that improves voice recognition and the acquisition of signs, and is fully adapted to many languages and sign dialects. Addressing such health and safety issues is essential to advancing the communication and optimization of this advanced technology.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Cervical Cancer Detection:SMOTE and Entropy Boosted Random Forest Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: One of the most severe diseases that affect women is cervical cancer, which occurs when cells in the cervix or lower section of the uterus grow abnormally and develop into a cancerous tumor. The papillomavirus, sometimes known as HPV, is the primary cause of this particular type of cancer. If this kind of cancer is not treated, it will spread quickly to other body parts and cause grave complications. This cancer has two extreme features: it shows no symptoms in its early stages, there's a higher possibility of being treatable. The PAP test, which looks for abnormalities in uterine cells under a microscope and may detect the disease if there are any alterations, is the independent screening and testing procedure used to identify this form of cancer. For instance, this can occasionally result in a false positive, meaning the patient is diagnosed with cancer when in fact they do not have it, or a false negative, meaning that during sample collection, abnormal cells were either absent or improperly collected, or both. To mitigate these drawbacks, alternative approaches are needed to improve accuracy and enable early diagnosis, which will boost treatment effectiveness and survival rates. This can only be achieved through computerized methods, particularly with machine learning algorithms that allow for increased accuracy and the integration of multiple data sets, including electronic health records, PAP test results, and HPV test results. Therefore, machine learning model is created in this research study for the early prediction of cervical cancer using the Cervical Cancer dataset from the UCI Repository. There are 32 risk factors associated with each of the four target variables in this dataset: Himmelmann, Schiller, Cytology, and Biopsy. The dataset has a class imbalance issue, meaning that one set of records is significantly higher than another, leading to a biassed outcome. Therefore, the SMOTE approach is used in this research work to prevent biassed results and to improve accuracy. Metrics including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score are used to assess how well algorithms work in detecting cervical cancer

articleTitle: Image Encryption Using Neural Network Based Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper introduces a unique image encryption methodology using the chaotic signals generated by a neural network for enhanced security. The proposed system employs a master-slave configuration where a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network acts as the master system for encryption, while the Hopfield neural network serves as the slave system generating the chaotic signal for decryption. The process of encryption involves the XOR operation between the input image and the chaotic signal generated by the master system. To ensure accurate synchronisation between the master-slave systems for decrypting the image, an Active Sliding Mode Controller (ASMC) is used which ensures robust convergence and minimal synchronisation error. Performance evaluation through histogram analysis shows that the proposed encryption method is more secure and efficient compared to the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) method.

articleTitle: Deepfake Voice Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Approach to Identifying Synthetic Audio
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Deepfake voice recognition has lately been one of the critical challenges in the domain of cybersecurity and digital forensics, as it has recently become increasingly used with deep learning models to create absolutely indistinguishable audio imitations. This paper proposes a CNN-based approach to detect and classify deepfake audio clips. The model is trained on an exhaustive dataset that includes both real and deepfake voice records, putting much attention into the difference between natural and manipulated speech patterns. Our approach is based on the spectrogram analysis-a method of audio signal processing by converting it into a visual format that the CNN then analyzes to extract and categorize features. We test the performance of this model, which has gone through rigorous training with an accuracy of 82.6% and a test loss of 0.386. Results indicate that the proposed CNN architecture successfully learns nuanced acoustic variations between real and synthetic voices, setting up a robust framework for the detection of deepfakes. Moreover, the generalizability of the model has been checked multiple times, keeping the training and validation metrics very close. Future works will further improve the detection accuracy by including more pre-processing techniques and increasing the dataset with more varieties of deepfake sources. The study therefore adds to the ever-increasing demand for reliable and capable tools in the identification of audio forgeries, which seriously threatens privacy, security, and integrity of information in our time.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Based Web Automation for Smart Power Supply Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Home automation is becoming increasingly important in today’s world, with new technologies focusing on providing better user experience and reduced energy consumption. Also, the opportunity of working from home is becoming more common in professional settings, creating a greater need for home automation. An important aspect of such systems is represented by the lighting system, which provides enhanced convenience and efficiency. The present paper focuses on the automation of lighting as a development process that can be done both locally and via the web. The fuzzy logic-based local automation requires three key inputs: the previous light intensity is between 0% - 100%, the relative work mode is between 0 to 24H, and the temperature is between 0°C to 40°C. Time is categorized into working, relaxing, and sleeping mode. The system optimizes lighting based on user behavior and environmental factors to increase energy efficiency. As lighting devices proliferate, power consumption rises. This paper designs an intelligent system using fuzzy logic to manage lighting in smart buildings. Inputs include light intensity measured by an LDR sensor, work culture based on daily phases, and human presence detected by a PIR sensor. The system increases and decreases lighting adjustment when the intensity and the work culture values differ and it sends the data to an ESP8266 Node Wi-Fi microcontroller through a monitoring that is used by the real-time monitoring via an IoT based Web Monitoring tool. Therefore, this system facilitates early warnings of changes in remote parameters, which allow adjustment of the lighting. It can be concluded from the results that the latter are moderate. Technological progress opens the possibility of creating customizable and automated home systems. Smart lighting is an essential part of such systems as it has many advantages, such as being automatic, customizable and user-friendly. The given study is devoted to the issue of the optimization of a home lighting system with the help of fuzzy logic.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Copper and Cobalt Loaded Multi-Patch Rectangular Antenna for Multi Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper provides an in-depth comparative analysis of the performance of multi-patch rectangular loop antennas utilizing different materials, specifically copper and cobalt, for the patches, and RT Duroid and Graphite as substrates, with a motivation on 5 GHz frequency applications. The study inspects antennas constructed with these varied materials, assessing key parameters such as return loss (S11), Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR), and radiation efficiency over a range of frequencies. The conclusions offer valuable insights into optimizing the design of high-performance multi-patch rectangular loop antennas for 5 GHz applications, assisting in the selection of materials to improve antenna performance.

articleTitle: Exploratory Analysis of Zero-Shot Lunar Crater Detection using SAM for Chandrayaan-2 Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper explores the application of a zero-shot lunar crater detection method based on the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for high-resolution Digital Terrain Model (DTM) images from ISRO’s Chandrayaan-II mission. A pre-trained transformer-based instance segmentation model, SAM, is used to segment and identify lunar craters without requiring training data. The proposed method is capable of detecting craters in varying crater sizes and shapes, highlighting its potential for generalizable planetary feature detection. This work investigates the applicability of general-purpose deep learning models in planetary exploration and offers insights for efficient lunar surface analysis.

articleTitle: Clustering-Based Multi-Crop Recommendation System for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Agriculture in India is an ancient and essential industry, providing food and livelihoods to millions. However, centuries of continuous land use without sufficient knowledge of soil properties have depleted soil nutrients, leading to declining crop yields. Limited adoption of modern agricultural practices further intensifies this issue, underscoring the need for precision agriculture. To address this, we analyzed a dataset containing soil nutrient content and key climatic factors such as temperature, humidity, and rainfall, enabling optimal crop recommendations to enhance farmers’ yields. Using cluster analysis, this paper identified similarities in crop requirements, promoting multi-cropping on the same land to boost productivity, especially for small-scale farmers. Among the models tested, the Random Forest and Naive Bayes algorithms showed remarkable effectiveness, achieving an accuracy of 99%.

articleTitle: Detecting Malicious Threats On Mobile Applications Using Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In Today scenario , Android is one of the most frequently used mobile operatings systems, thus it is a priority for advanced threat actors and hackers. Malicious code is often found in Android applications to which security solutions have a problem of identifying the threats. Today’s Android malware is sophisticated enough that it can avoid most detection .Therefore, machine learning is more efficient in stopping a large number of diverse contemporary threats to Android devices. These machine learning methods essentially first rely on the detection of sequential patterns of malicious behaviors, and secondly, distinguish between existing and new types of threats that have previously exhibited typical and atypical behavior. Our proposed approach builds on Ensemble learning where the methods include Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, Logistic regression and XGBoost to bolster the detection abilities of the model. This methodology serves to enhance the specific model performance on identifying known malware .

articleTitle: AI-Based Posture Correction, Real-Time Exercise Tracking and Feedback using Pose Estimation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Physical activity is an essential component of physical and mental health-being. Although physical activity offers numerous advantages, maintaining proper posture could be difficult, especially when it comes to complex movements or poses. This task is even challenging for the ones who exercise at home, those who have disabilities, or social anxiety. In order to deal with this issue, this work proposes an AI gym tracker app powered by advanced pose estimation technology through OpenCV and Mediapipe which are two popular frameworks being used in computer vision to access and solve several real-life problems through pose-estimation. This paper describes an AI-powered gym tracker app built with MediaPipe and OpenCV. It uses real-time pose estimation and joint angle calculation to provide feedback on exercise form as well as expanded rep count. This application employs a unique method by using dynamic angle thresholds and joint distance computations to provide precise feedback about user posture. It demonstrates the application's effectiveness in assisting users in maintaining proper form and tracking their workout progress by demonstrating a counter. Future work is to broaden its functionality to embrace more exercises and to further add other forms of decision feedback system, thus exploring the possible incorporation of this application into various fitness apps which would in-turn enhance the overall experience of the users.

articleTitle: Improved EEG-Based Epileptic Seizure Classification Using Fusion of Machine Learning Model with Statistical Feature Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, often diagnosed through the analysis of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. In this study, we propose a machine learning-based approach to classify EEG data into different brain states, focusing on epileptic seizure detection. Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is employed to extract relevant time-frequency domain features from the EEG signals. Additionally, a set of statistical features—mean, standard deviation, variance, energy, entropy, coefficient of variation, root mean square, skewness, and kurtosis are incorporated to further enhance classification performance. Various machine learning models such as Random Forest, KNN, and LightGBM were evaluated. Results show that combining DWT with statistical features significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of the classification compared to using DWT alone. For example, the Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 84.85% with DWT alone, which increased to 84.88% when combined with statistical features. Similarly, LightGBM improved from 84.87% to 85.10% in accuracy. This approach could serve as a valuable tool for aiding in the diagnosis and treatment of epilepsy.

articleTitle: Forecasting Stock Market Volatility Using XGBoost: A Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Forecasting stock market volatility presents significant challenges and opportunities for both practitioners and researchers in the financial sector. This paper explores the application of eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), an advanced ensemble machine learning technique, to predict stock market volatility using time series data from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI). Our methodology utilizes past price data containing open, high, low, and close prices, along with capacity and adjusted close values, to capture the underlying patterns indicative of future market movements. We preprocess this data using techniques like normalization and feature engineering to enhance the predictive capabilities of our model. The XGBoost model is upgraded through extensive hyperparameter tuning and is considered in contrast to customary measurements like Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Blunder (RMSE), and the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score to survey its precision and adequacy. Our results demonstrate that XGBoost can effectively capture the complexities and non-linear relationships inherent in stock price movements, outperforming standard benchmark models. The findings suggest that machine learning models, particularly those based on tree ensemble methods like XGBoost, provide a robust tool for financial analysts seeking to mitigate risks and capture opportunities in volatile markets. This paper contributes to the ongoing discourse in financial econometrics by confirming the viability of advanced machine learning techniques in forecasting market dynamics, thus offering valuable insights for both theoretical advancement and practical application in financial forecasting.

articleTitle: Navigation On Mobile Computing Devices with A Walking Using Object-Oriented Techniques to Communicate Stick
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Moving around in their surroundings is challenging for elderly people and people with visual impairments. The majority of functional sticks in use today are not intelligent and lack an innate ability to recognize obstacles. In an effort to address this issue, mobility and orientation specialists who assist the blind by teaching them to move freely and safely using their remaining senses are brought in. They can navigate around obstacles with the aid of guidance dogs as well. These techniques have drawbacks, such as the dogs' inability to comprehend complicated instructions, the high cost of maintaining these trained dogs, and the need to hire an expert. In light of the aforementioned difficulties, the "Smart walking stick" has become a potential answer. The "Mobile based walking stick" is a useful mobility aid with the capacity to call a relative who can help in the event of an accident, detect obstacles above ground level and pits using ultrasonic sensors, recognize when a collision has occurred, and call the user's mobile phone if it has been misplaced to share the location's GPS for use with GSM connectivity and to share with the user's mention contacts. With some visually disabled people as test subjects, a test case was run, and 95% of the time it was successful.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Standard Ternary Inverter Architectures based on 18nm FinFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: As modern VLSI circuits encounter growing challenges in power consumption and interconnect complexity, ternary logic emerges as a promising alternative to traditional binary logic by introducing a third logic state. This enhancement enables higher data density and more efficient circuit designs, significantly reducing the number of interconnections and gates required. This research aims to evaluate and compare the performance of three FinFET-based ternary inverter architectures by analyzing key metrics such as power consumption, propagation delay, and power-delay product (PDP). Using simulations conducted in the Cadence Virtuoso tool, the study reveals that the design proposed in [14] excels in power efficiency, while the design in [13] achieves a lower propagation delay. The findings highlight the potential of ternary logic, combined with FinFET technology, to improve energy efficiency and performance in future VLSI circuits, making it well-suited for low-power and high-speed applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Design Analysis of Different Radome Shapes for Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: RADOMES are essential components in modern communication systems, providing protection for antennas against environmental factors such as rain, snow, and wind while preserving signal quality. This paper examines the design and performance of various radome shapes for horn antennas, focusing on their impact on the radiation pattern and overall signal integrity. Using CST Studio for simulation, the study explores how different radome configurations affect electromagnetic transparency and mechanical protection, aiming to minimize signal distortion, reflection, and absorption. The comparative analysis offers insights into optimizing radome designs to enhance antenna performance in applications such as aerospace, satellites, and ground-based systems.

articleTitle: Effective Adaptable Framework for Security of IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) becomes the most demanding technology over the past few years. IoT is the basic need of daily life. The security of these devices is very important because they contain large files of sensitive data, the exposure of these devices can be fatal. To ensure the security of different types of IoT devices, we have designed a problem for optimization of weights in this work. The operational goal of this work is to protect different IoT devices alogwith determining a balance between resource and device usage. This framework includes resources and transfers the requirements of heterogeneous IoT devices and modifies different image and implementations using Hungarian algorithm. To attain the objective, five different ways are described to solve the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Extensive testing is done to find the best trade with different stocks and weights. The proposed framework is also compared to random greedy methods. The benchmark results show that the proposed system has been modified to secure the system based on IoT while offering better performance and results. Compared to the random method, the proposed method yielded an average of 3% and 13% improvement and in 11% and 17% greedy approach and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Ensemble Based MRI Analysis for Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The neurodegenerative disorder Alzheimer’s disease is indicated by cognitive deficits and memory loss. Early identification and diagnosis of the disease contribute positively to therapeutic intervention opportunities, and can improve patient outcomes following diagnosis. Structural brain abnormalities linked with Alzheimer’s can be reliably measured through magnetic resonance imaging, making it a strong imaging modality for cognitive impairment assessment, including Alzheimer’s. This study develops an ensemble learning strategy to diagnose patients with Alzheimer’s using MRI data. Specifically, an ensemble strategy uses the strengths of multiple less complex machine learning models to improve predictive accuracy and robustness locally or across populations, as compared to using a single model. The proposed ensemble diagnostic model utilizes pre-processed MRI images in order to extract relevant features of interest, and the software stack publishes the assessment of various machine learning models. The proposed method exhibits key performance metrics as accuracy-0.99, F1 score-0.98, recall-1.00 and precision-0.96. It shows that ensemble learning is a very powerful machine learning method to use for machine learning predictions when compared to traditional and individual approaches.

articleTitle: An Optimized Inverse Neural Network Control Augmented with Feedback PI Controller for Time-Varying Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Linear proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers often fail to provide adequate control performance for nonlinear and time-varying systems due to their constant parametric nature. To address the challenges posed by nonlinear and time-varying systems in their regulation, intelligent controllers using neural networks (NN) and fuzzy logic have been vastly investigated. Out of these techniques, NN-based controllers are more popular for the design of indirect adaptive control schemes owing to their immense learning capability. Yet, these NN controllers may fail to perform well if their hyperparameters, typically learning rate and initial weights, are not designed properly. The control performance may worsen if these NNs fail to mimic or learn the system's dynamics. To address this issue, the current work explores the possibility of employing bio-inspired optimization to tune the essential hyperparameters of NN, along with the inclusion of a PI controller in the loop to compensate for the unidentified dynamics. Through the extensive simulation studies carried out in this work, it was found that the learning capability of the INN assisted by a feedback PI controller, i.e. (INN+PI) controller, could achieve superior performance compared to INN only. This paper also compares the ability of the designed INN+PI controller with only the PI controller in terms of set point tracking, the controller’s output on the basis of significant decrement in MSE and IAE, and elucidates the simulation results.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Based Multiband Microstrip Patch Antenna with Defective Ground
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In this research a dual band microstrip patch antenna, which resonates on IEEE 802.11a 2.45 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi bands, is proposed. The patch is slotted at two opposite edges to obtain the dual band characteristics. The size of ground plane has been reduced and a split ring resonator has been incorporated to enhance the gain and bandwidth of the proposed antenna. Initially, the patch antenna resonates at 5.8 GHz with gain and bandwidth of 6 dBi and 290 MHz, respectively. Also, an additional resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz is generated when two slots are added at the patch's two opposing edges. This resonant frequency’s gain and impedance bandwidth are, respectively, 345 MHz and 10.5 dBi. When ground plane is reduced in size and a split ring resonator is incorporated in the ground plane, the initial resonant frequency gets shifted to 5 GHz, along with betterment in gain and impedance bandwidth at this resonant frequency. Now the designed antenna resonates at 5 GHz with 410 MHz impedance bandwidth and 6.5 dBi gain. FR-4 substrate has been selected to design this proposed antenna, with a commercially available electromagnetic simulator, HFSS.

articleTitle: Analysing the Identification Approaches of Deep Fake Images and Videos Encapsulated in Fake Contents Available on Social Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century is characterized by the emergence of AI tools, which have become essential in today's diverse application landscape. These tools find utility across various sectors such as research, customer service, medical sciences, education, software industries, and factories. AI has the capability to generate images and videos that closely resemble reality, often making it challenging to distinguish between authentic and altered content. In contemporary usage, artificial intelligence software is frequently employed in creating WhatsApp videos and Instagram reels, blurring the line between reality and fabrication. Consequently, there is a tendency for such manipulated content to circulate unchecked, masquerading as genuine news. In this research paper, we aim to examine instances of ostensibly authentic news that have been tampered with using image editing tools. Accurate identification of such manipulated content is crucial, particularly as it may serve as essential legal evidence.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of a six phase High Speed Homopolar Inductor Machine for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Recently research has been going on in high power density high-speed electrical machines in small aircrafts and unmanned vehicles and fighter planes as auxiliary power applications such as capacitor charging, and flywheel energy storage systems. The requirement for electrical power sources in such vehicles is small size and less weight. A Homopolar Inductor machine (HSHIM) is a machine with special construction which can be operated at very high speed up to 100000 RPM. This paper presents the implementation of modeling and analysis of a High -Speed Homopolar Inductor Machine(HSHIM) in MATLAB. All the dynamics of HSHIM have been modelled using mathematical equations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Pediatric Pneumonia Detection in Children using Fine-tuned NasNetMobile Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Pediatric pneumonia is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in children worldwide. Traditional methods for detecting the disease are time-consuming, thereby necessitating automated detection methods. Hence, the paper fine-tunes the light-weight NasNetMobile model architecture using multiple normalization approaches and six recent activation functions like Swish, HardSwish, Mish, etc. to enhance model performance and generalization in the efficient detection of pediatric pneumonia in children. The work also conducts a comparative analysis of six state-of-the-art model CNN model architectures to prove the efficacy of the proposed model. The outcomes show that fine-tuned NasNetMobile model using the Mish activation function, combined with batch normalization and dropout, outperforms other configurations with an F-score of 92%.

articleTitle: Advances in Deep Learning for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Anomaly detection in multivariate time series data is essential across a range of industries, including finance, healthcare, and manufacturing, where timely identification of unusual patterns can prevent significant operational disruptions. This study explores the applications of deep learning methods including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Autoencoders, Hybrid models, and Transformers in time series anomaly detection. By analyzing data collected from various sensors that monitor key parameters such as temperature, pressure, vibration, and sound, this research addresses the complexities associated with detecting deviations from normal behavior in high-dimensional datasets. We deeply analyze the methodologies, datasets, and evaluation metrics employed in existing studies, focusing on the comparative performance of these techniques. This review also highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, providing a detailed understanding of their applicability to different types of time series data. By synthesizing insights from numerous research contributions, we aim to chart the current landscape of deep learning-based anomaly detection, uncover key challenges, and suggest potential directions for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: Analysis of CSA Tuned FONPID Controller Using Various Integral Based Metrices for Three Link Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Four various fractional-order nonlinear proportional-integral-derivative (FONPID) controllers are compared in this paper. They were all tuned using the Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA) based on various performance metrics, including Integral Absolute Error (IAE), Integral Square Error (ISE), Integral Time Square Error (ITSE) and Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). In particular, a three-link robotic manipulator is used in the research to assess how these performance indices affect the overall control accuracy and stability of a nonlinear multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system. To assess control accuracy, trajectory tracking performance, extensive simulations were run. The outcomes show that the system responsiveness, and computational efficiency all differ significantly depending on the performance parameter selected for the FONPID controller optimization. The study emphasizes the benefits of applying CSA for FONPID controller optimization and offers insightful information on tuning techniques for intricate MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Secure Electoral Voting System Using Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The integrity of electoral systems is paramount in ensuring democratic processes. This paper explores the use of homomorphic encryption (HE) in electoral voting systems, providing a robust solution for maintaining voter privacy while enabling transparent and verifiable vote tallying. The study delves into cryptographic protocols such as Paillier and ElGamal encryption schemes, emphasizing their mathematical foundations and applicability to voting systems. The proposed system architecture integrates HE to achieve secure and efficient vote tallying. This paper also discusses the challenges and potential solutions associated with implementing HE in large-scale elections, followed by a detailed analysis of results and conclusions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Accident Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: With the growing population and the consequent surge in vehicular traffic, there is an urgent need for heightened safety measures. Addressing this challenge requires the integration of advanced systems equipped with highly sensitive sensors to proactively mitigate the risk of accidents. Ensuring vehicle reliability is paramount, leading to the incorporation of microcontrollers within each vehicle. These microcontrollers enable seamless data storage in cloud-based platforms and utilize SIM technology for uninterrupted communication and data transmission. Beyond data aggregation, these systems play a critical role in swiftly guiding individuals to emergency services in the event of an accident. Additionally, they provide crucial information and assistance to both drivers and passengers, both before and after an accident, thereby enhancing overall safety measures. This comprehensive approach not only prioritizes accident prevention but also ensures rapid and effective response mechanisms, thereby reducing potential risks and elevating overall road safety standards.

Author Keywords: Global system for mobile communication component

articleTitle: High Resolution Image Upsampler for Lung Adenocarcinoma diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Lung Adenocarcinoma is a kind of NSCLC (non-small cell lung cancer) which is the most occurring form of lung cancer. It progresses in the epithelial cells that coat the Alveoli sacs of the lungs. Adenocarcinoma refers to cancer formed in mucus secreting cells, thus giving it its name. Patients suffering from this disease shows a combination of symptoms such as pneumonia, coughing up blood, fatigue and weight loss which covers a wide range of unrelated manifestation leading the disease to go unnoticed and often causing fatality. Just like any other cancer, Lung Adenocarcinoma desires early and accurate diagnosis. Current methods include various forms of imaging techniques such as PET scan, biopsy procedures and genetic testing. Diagnosis is followed by a plethora of treatment options such as Chemotherapy, Targeted therapy and Immunotherapy. Despite such efficacious treatment techniques, their effect entirely relies on the stage of diagnosis and its accuracy. Keeping such dearth in mind, we put forward a high resolution upsampled image generator which is packed with combinations of advanced neural network incorporating Machine learning model and techniques such as GANs (Generative Adversarial Network). This platform utilizes pathological data from several trusted sources to develop the AI model which as a result will increase the accuracy of biopsy diagnosis. Trained on the dataset that was carefully acquired and the initial 750 samples were augmented generating the final dataset of 4500+ image samples using the ‘Augmentor’ package in python, the model delivers superior results than current diagnosis methods while simultaneously improving biopsy performance. It guarantees model stability to variations which is achieved through minimizing loss function and parameter tuning while enhancing computational efficiency. This development may eventually result in filling the gap in current diagnosis methods by improving its results manifold.

articleTitle: Advancements in Credit Scoring, Profit Scoring, and Portfolio Optimization for P2P Lending
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The Peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platform allows borrowers to connect directly with lenders outside traditional banking systems. Therefore, for the sustainability of these platforms, they must accurately assess the credit risk and profitability of the loans. Various credit scoring techniques, including Logistic Regression, neural networks, and ensemble methods, can be used to estimate the likelihood of borrower default. It is imperative to analyze the profit the lenders generated and enhance the credit scoring so that the investors face minimum loss. Once the profit analysis is done, then it is crucial to advise the investors about the portfolio of loans. This paper presents recent credit scoring, profit scoring, and portfolio optimization trends for P2P lending. We highlight the significant issues in incorporating machine learning models into credit scoring systems. The analysis emphasizes the need for a data-driven approach to perfecting lending practices, thus benefiting both borrowers and investors in the rapidly changing P2P landscape.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Approaches to Agricultural Intelligence: U-Net, YOLO, and Random Forest in Practice
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper seeks to implement and test advanced precision agricultural monitoring and detection systems derived from machine learning, remote sensing, and sensor technologies to improve pest detection, crop yields assessment, and animal husbandry management practices. The approach involves an automated and hierarchical framework integrating cutting edge machine learning technologies with fine spatial resolution remote sensing images and sensors. For instance, the authors apply CNN (convolutional neural networks) for pest identification; the deep learning models trained on Sentinel-2 images serve as yield predictors; UWB location coordinates and accelerometric measures combined form livestock behavior monitoring. This methodology encompasses the stages of implementation, testing and finally verification of the model. A variety of machine learning systems such as Faster-PestNet or deep semantic segmentation algorithms process data while remote sensing and the sensors’ data were used in predictions and classifications. This allows using different performance measures such as accuracy, precision recall rates and RMSE (root mean square error) to test the systems.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Electric Vehicles Charging-Discharging Topologies for Sustainable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained immense popularity in recent times owing to the decrease in conventional energy resource reserves and the concurrent threat to the environment caused from the harmful discharge of IC engine vehicles. EVs are mainly divided into the following three categories: pure electrical vehicles or battery electric vehicles, hybrid electrical vehicles, and fuel cell electrical vehicles. All these classifications have certain advantages and drawbacks associated with them. Based on the associated advantages and disadvantages, various aspects of EV performance have been scrutinized namely, design optimization, transmission performance optimization, battery management system (BMS) and charging technology to name a few. While all the abovementioned aspects affect the EV performance critically, BMS and charging technology have been the main area of concern for design engineers and researchers. Herein, two major charging topologies are prevalent, i.e. vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and grid-to-vehicle (G2V). Moreover, a third and fourth scheme of operation, namely, vehicle-to-home (V2H) and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) topology respectively, is also gaining importance off-late. With this view, the present manuscript aims to categorize, engulf and encapsulate the different EVs along with the existing charging technologies in EVs and BMS. This shall make the topic at hand easier to comprehend for the prospective future researchers.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Prediction and Analysis of Financial Distress
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The importance of financial distress prediction (FDP) in addressing corporate financial risk management has grown over the last decade. The majority of earlier studies in this area attempted to address financial issues and bankruptcy forecasts through the use of AI technologies or conventional bankruptcy prediction models. Investors' decisions can be influenced by news of financial difficulty, and relying too much on the opinions of financial analysts or one's own subjective assessment can lead to poor decision-making. As a result, this study aims to provide a fresh, objective model of FDP. This study evaluate three ML models: LSTM, RF, and KNN, measuring their performance using critical metrics like F1Score, AUC, Precision, Accuracy, and Recall. A following models are implemented on the NYSE and NASDAQ from 1999 to 2018, utilizing a dataset comprising 8,262 firms. Our results indicate that the LSTM model significantly outperforms both RF and KNN, achieving an F1-score 77.2% and an AUC 83.2%. These findings suggest that LSTM is a superior approach for financial distress prediction, highlighting its potential for enhancing risk assessment frameworks in financial analytics.

articleTitle: From Manual to Machine: How AI is Redefining Web Scraping for Superior Efficiency: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Web Scraping involves the use of bots for the purpose of extracting data from the online web. To extract such data, the web scraper must conduct at least 3 different steps, i.e., collect the necessary links from the web, extract data using the provided links, and save the information in a neatly organized CSV file or database. However, traditional methods to accomplish these steps have faced many difficulties, such as anti-scraping measures and website changes. To tackle these difficulties and to accomplish the steps in a more rapid yet advanced way, Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be utilized. As of mid-2024, the rapid development and improvement of AI has resulted in its integration into many businesses and educational institutions. The current state of AI is remarkably advanced that it can be integrated in about any field and sector available. In this paper, the researcher defined the term Web Scraping, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, and Machine Learning, explained the use of AI in Web Scraping including its importance and potential, and the understanding of ethical web scraping practices. This literature review indicated that the integrated use of AI improves the performance of Web Scraping compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: The Rise of Intelligence: A Comprehensive Review on AI and AI Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) technologies, focusing on their impact in driving AI automation across diverse sectors with a special emphasis on robotics. As AI continues to evolve, its integration into automation systems has revolutionized industries, enhancing efficiency, precision, and decision-making. The role of AI automation in robotics is critically examined, covering key architectural frameworks that enable autonomous operation and intelligent decision-making. Furthermore, the security aspects associated with AI in robotics, identifying attack surfaces and potential vulnerabilities has been analysed. This review highlights the transformative potential of AI automation while addressing the challenges and security concerns that accompany its deployment in modern systems, particularly in robotics.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment and Enhancement of Transformer Models for Effective Text Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper emphases onto development and enhancement of text generation models using transformer architectures, specifically GPT-2. The designed system focuses on three key models: (1) a baseline GPT-2 model, (2) an optimized GPT-2 model incorporating various enhancements, and (3) an updated optimized model fine-tuned on new datasets compared with a custom GPT implementation-AuThorGPT. Techniques such as perplexity evaluation and temperature scaling will be integrated to refine the model’s performance. The ultimate goal is to generate text in the style of specific training data, such as Shakespeare’s works, while continuously fine-tuning the model with additional data to track and analyze improvements in output quality.

articleTitle: An Efficient Model for Identifying Human Behaviour using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The extensive domain of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is dedicated to the identification of specific human actions or movements through the use of sensor data. Furthermore, it is capable of detecting and distinguishing human activity, as well as disseminating information about the detected motion or activity. Skeleton coordinates are employed by the HAR program to identify human body activity or motion. To be more precise, this application serves as an instrument for the analysis of human activity and is capable of automatically detecting the following activities: standing, sitting, lying down, walking, stairs, and walking. This paper introduces a hybrid model that employs deep learning to detect human activity. The model includes a diverse array of layer counts and the six most common activities. Furthermore, the proposed model will recognize behaviours such as walking, standing, sitting, lying down, falling, walking, and walking on staircases. The individual's activities will be consistently monitored by the proposed model, which will also issue appropriate notifications. However, this model is capable of detecting human activity in real time using even the most basic computer, in contrast to other models that require extremely potent CPU specifications to function in real time and rely on sensors to detect activity. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel hybrid deep learning model for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) that effectively detects six common activities using skeletal coordinates on fundamental computing systems without the need for sensors. It operates across a variety of camera angles without the need for code adjustments, as it seamlessly integrates with CCTV systems. The model is deployable online, guaranteeing accessibility through web browsers, and its accuracy can be improved by utilising real-world datasets such as CCTV footage. This method expands the applicability of HAR to a wider range of applications, including healthcare, smart homes, surveillance, sports, and more, with minimal computational requirements.

articleTitle: Effective Machine Learning-Based Predictive Analytics for Loan Default Prediction in Banking Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: These days, a crucial topic is the early prediction of loan failure in banks. Customer loan default may be predicted using a variety of statistical and AI classification methods. This paper introduces a machine learning-based predictive analytics model aimed at improving loan default prediction in the banking sector by leveraging open P2P loan data from Lending Club. To improve the precision and consistency of predictions, the model uses state-of-the-art ML methods, namely RF. By analyzing critical borrower information such as credit history, loan purpose, and debt status, the model identifies high-risk borrowers with greater precision. The study evaluates a performance of different ML models, including LR, DT, and SVM, but identifies RF as the most effective, demonstrating superior metrics with 89% accuracy, 99.5% sensitivity, and 80.3% specificity. These results highlight the model’s ability to not only predict defaults accurately but also reduce false positives and negatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Early Detection and Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease Stages Using Deep Learning and LIME for Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The issue of transparency in diagnostic methods has been a crucial challenge in Alzheimer’s Disease detection. This paper focuses on analyzing state-of-art deep learning algorithms namely, customized convolutional network, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 for detecting Alzheimer’s disease. The work also focuses on analyzing the transparency and decision-making capabilities of these models by using the Explainable AI tool, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations, for clinicians and patients. The learnings and decision outputs obtained from these convolutional models are related and explained using LIME, where ResNet and DenseNet lead to efficient solutions with appropriate feature extraction and importance provided in LIME visualization. This explication of the model’s decision-making process affected by LIME can improve diagnostic accuracy and foster trust that can offer a great chance for the medical experts to offer better care for patients, who are suffering from Alzheimer’s Disease.

articleTitle: An Assessment of Several Electric Vehicle Motors Performance for AI Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
