abstract: As the global automotive industry transitions to more ecologically friendly and sustainable forms of transportation, electric automobiles, or EVs, have shown a great deal of promise as a replacement for conventional internal combustion engine vehicles. The electric motors in electric vehicles (EVs) need to function well for the vehicles to be popular and generally accepted. The performance analysis of this study comprehensively examines the various types of electric motors used in electric vehicles, such as permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), induction motors (IM), and switching resistance motors (SRM). The first section of the study provides a thorough overview of the basic ideas, design, and operation of all types of motors. The focus lies on providing an overview of their benefits, limitations, and appropriateness for different automotive uses.Compact size, light weight , durability and compatibility with regenerative braking is focused . It is found that 45-50 % vehicles uses permanent magnet synchronous motor ,30-35 % uses Induction motors,10-15 % uses synchronous reluctance motor. 5-10 % uses switched reluctance motor,1-5% Axial Flux reluctance motor,5-7 % brush less DC motor and transverse flux motor is less that 1%.

articleTitle: CNN Image Forgery Detection: Machine Learning Improves Photojournalism Accuracy and Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to address the rising problem of picture modification and fraud, especially in the field of photojournalism, where the ability to recognize changed photos is essential to preserving faith in digital technology. By employing CNN-based approaches, the created forgery detection system exhibits its capacity to reliably discern between actual and AI-generated photos, reaching a balanced classification of 49% and 50%, respectively, with low misclassification. The purpose of this research is to investigate the development of digital picture forensics by using both conventional methods and contemporary innovations such as blockchain and deep learning. In order to achieve a higher level of detection accuracy, the suggested system makes use of machine learning models, such as transfer learning using pretrained models like ImageNet. The findings demonstrate that the system is capable of generalization and has a limited amount of overfitting, as seen by the high training accuracy of 98.44% and the validation accuracy of 98.92%. It is accepted that there is a need for future improvements in scalability, robustness to adversarial assaults, and interpretability, despite the fact that the findings have been somewhat encouraging. In order to successfully battle increasingly complex picture forgeries, future breakthroughs in digital image forensics will need cooperation between the government, industry, and academic institutions.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Education by Enhancing Security and Integrity with Blockchain and Fungible Token-Based Academic Assessments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The rising significance of blockchain technology in academia is underscored by its potential to solve pressing challenges in data security, transparency, and management within educational institutions. The current research delves into creating a secure and transparent academic assessment framework leveraging Ethereum smart contracts. Through the Ethereum blockchain, this research tackles crucial concerns such as safeguarding data privacy, ensuring interoperability, and enhancing user experience which are inherent into blockchain technology. The proposed framework employs role-specific access controls, fortifies data integrity and privacy, and adheres to academic regulations. Further, it prioritizes developing an intuitive interface to improve user interaction. The study’s thorough methodology encompasses blockchain tools, system workflows, validation techniques, and a layered architecture. Implementation and testing results indicate the system’s effectiveness in providing a fraud-resistant, efficient, and accountable academic assessment solution, paving the way for future advancements and the adoption of blockchain in education.

articleTitle: Weed Identification using Deep Learning and Meta-heuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Agriculture holds crucial economic significance and is vital for sustaining growing populations’ dietary requirements. With a substantial increase in population size, ensuring food security has emerged as a pertinent issue. The adoption of smart farming practices has become imperative to meet these objectives. This paper focuses on weed identification systems within smart farming, proposing metaheuristic-optimized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. These hybrid models are empowered by algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) and Jaya Algorithm (JAYA). These models were benchmarked against existing transfer-learning-based approaches. Notably, the GA-optimized covolutional architecture exhibited superior performance (accuracy of 96.57%) compared to pre-trained models, underscoring the effectiveness of metaheuristic optimization techniques in enhancing weed identification accuracy. This study encapsulates a comprehensive exploration of unveiling deep learning techniques to revolutionize the weed identification task.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Airborne Contaminant Spread with Cloud-Connected Sensors and Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The rapid dispersal of contaminants in the air poses serious threats to human and environmental health. By combining sensors linked to the cloud with a deep learning (DL) model built on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, this research proposes a novel way to address this problem. It will help with risk mitigation and proactive decision-making by predicting how airborne pollutants will disperse. The proposed method relies on real-time data gathered from dispersed sensors placed in key areas. These sensors provide data on air quality metrics to a central cloud platform that is analyzed in real-time. Using this data, the LSTM model may be trained to understand the dynamics of contamination distribution over time and identify patterns and relationships. The LSTM model captures complex interactions between pollutant dispersion and various environmental parameters to predict future spread trajectories. The effectiveness of proposed approach is by conducting thorough experiments and validating them against historical contamination data. The considerably outperforms conventional approaches by providing precise and timely estimates of the spread of airborne contaminants. To lessen the impact of possible contamination exposure concerns, these predictions may provide stakeholders with the data need to act swiftly, such as by releasing public health warnings or modifying ventilation systems.

articleTitle: Nanotechnology's Potential in Advancing Renewable Energy Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Renewable energy technologies are crucial for addressing the energy problems we face today. One promising area of research is nanotechnology, which is proliferating and offers new solutions. This paper explores how nanotechnology can help develop renewable energy across various applications. By taking advantage of the unique properties of nanomaterials—such as their large surface area, adjustable optical and electrical features, and better catalytic activity— researchers and engineers can create advanced materials and devices that perform much better and more efficiently. Nanomaterials can enhance batteries, supercapacitors, and other energy storage devices by improving the materials used for electrodes and electrolytes, as well as by creating nanostructured designs. Additionally, advances in fuel cell technology, such as using nanoparticles as catalysts for efficient hydrogen production, show the wide range of possibilities for nanotechnology in renewable energy. This paper highlights the important role of nanotechnology in speeding up the transition to sustainable energy sources by reviewing current research and development efforts. Nanotechnology is becoming an essential part of our approach to tackling global warming and restoring the natural balance.

articleTitle: Analysis of factors affecting the future of the Game industry through Machine learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The video game industry is a significant economic force, generating billions of dollars in revenue annually. This paper analyses the factors influencing consumer preferences for different types of video games, focusing on platform availability, pricing, game genres, and evolving market trends. Data was collected through a survey of over 250 respondents, capturing demographic attributes and gaming preferences. Machine learning techniques, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, and LightGBM, were applied to predict platform preferences and recommend game genres based on age. The Decision Tree model outperformed others with an accuracy of 99.98%, demonstrating its suitability for both tasks. This study provides actionable insights into consumer behaviour, emphasizing the role of brand reputation, marketing efforts, and franchise value in shaping game success. These findings aim to inform game developers and publishers in crafting personalized, data-driven strategies to enhance player engagement and satisfaction.

articleTitle: An Analysis on Machine Learning Based Predictive Maintenance for Power Plants Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Electricity and energy systems experts have a significant issue when trying to forecast output from combined cycle power plants. This research aims at application of artificial intelligence methods for improving predictions for maintenance and power generation in nuclear power plants. In this analysis, different Machine learning (ML) models that are DNN, MLRP, Gradient Boosting, and RNN, are explored using the dataset of the CCPP with features including the exhaust vacuum, ambient temperature, ambient pressure, relative humidity, and net electrical energy output that amounts to 9,568 hourly measurements. The models’ performances are evaluated using statistics like RMSE, MAE, and the coefficient of determination of the models (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Findings show that the RNN model has the overall better fit by being able to achieve the highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0. 999 in the current analysis and hence better predictive ability than all the models being compared as well as the MLRP model with the lowest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0. 016. It provides an opportunity for a comparative analysis of how ML contributes to improving the predictive maintenance and operation of nuclear power systems and overcoming issues related to the handling of high volumes of data and the stability of station operations.

articleTitle: Forecasting Global Energy Consumption Trends: A Statistical Analysis of Low-Carbon Transition Using ARIMA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This study uses statistical approaches to investigate worldwide energy usage patterns. It assesses 116 countries and eight energy sources using data from Our World in Data, which spans 1965 to 2022. The report examines global energy trends since 1965, highlighting a significant decrease in fossil fuel consumption for the next 10 years. We have used ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) time series model, forecasting low-carbon energy use over the next decade. This comprehensive approach provides policymakers, industry, and stakeholders with vital insights, allowing them to make more informed decisions in pursuit of a sustainable energy future. Furthermore, improved analytical approaches provide a credible means of forecasting global energy consumption trends, which is critical for developing successful plans to promote renewable energy and reduce carbon emissions. With the growing need to battle climate change and safeguard our energy supply, it is critical to quickly transition to renewable energy sources. This change can be made with confidence if we use cutting-edge analytical techniques. This will result in a more resilient and ecologically enduring energy system for future generations at work.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Based Multiband Antenna for Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This research study introduces a multiband monopole antenna design that utilizes the (MTM) loading approach, for enhance efficiency, bandwidth of the antenna. Metamaterial integration allows significant antenna size reduction and frequency downshifting, enabling operation at lower frequencies while maintaining a compact design. The proposed antenna comprises a microstrip line monopole enhanced with an E slotted MTM design with T shaped structure included inside the patch which significantly enhances the performance of the proposed antenna. The MTM unit cell includes a transmission line with patches embedded with "E" shaped slots and rectangular horizontal slots along the feedline. Symmetrically loaded on both sides of the monopole antenna the MTM enables size reduction by lowering frequencies and achieving resonances. Fabricated on a polyamide substrate the antenna occupies a footprint of 10 × 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and functions across five frequencies; 2.8, 3.07 3.19, 3.4 and 6.4 GHz catering to applications such as Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) Wireless Fidelity (WiFi) and Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) all pertinent to IoT communications. A physical prototype of the antenna is. Validated through measurements based on simulation results. The efficiency hovers close, to an estimated 96% across the spectrum.

articleTitle: Effective Resource Utilization in Hadoop Using Ganglia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The exponential growth of big data has led to the widespread adoption of Hadoop clusters for storing and processing large volumes of data. Efficient management of resources within these clusters is crucial for achieving optimal performance and cost efficiency. This research paper explores the use of Hadoop and Ganglia for monitoring and optimizing resource utilization in Hadoop clusters. The study demonstrates that leveraging Hadoop and Ganglia is an effective strategy for improving cluster performance and resource efficiency. Results show significant enhancements in cluster performance and resource utilization, highlighting the importance of proactive resource management in Hadoop environments.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing as a Strategy for Robust Routing in Mobile Ad-hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In this study, we check the performance of traditional AODV (Ad-hoc On-Demand Distance Vector), MAODV (Multicast AODV), and a proposed Simulated Annealing (SA)-Optimized Routing protocol in a Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET). A python-based simulation was used to compare these protocols performance in terms of packets sent, packets received, latency, and throughput under dynamic network conditions. These results shows that SA-optimized routing consistently gives improved performance then AODV and MAODV in all performance metrics, achieving significantly higher packet delivery rates and lower latency. In SA-optimized routing adapts effectively to changing network conditions by exploring next to optimal routes early in the simulation and converging to optimal routes over time. This adaptability leads to better throughput, particularly in scenarios with high node mobility, making the SA-optimized routing protocol a more robust way for MANET environments.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Forecasting Financial Market Trends and Volatility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The existing culture where information is the key source of making financial decisions has placed emphasis on the relationship of sentiment and market as most important as ever. This paper looks specifically at the combination of top-notch ML and SA methods for the purpose of exploring up and coming avenues in the transformation of the fluctuations in the financial market. The purpose of this research is to find out how sentiment analysis and cutting-edge ML methods may work together to predict the direction and volatility of financial market movements. With the help of 42,110 daily samples of financial news, the study investigates the significance of the sentiment to the market and proves the superiority of LSTM networks over RNN and GRU networks. The research shows that LSTM has better prediction accuracy than other methods with a R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 97.9 and MAE of 17.689, according to a thorough performance assessment that uses important metrics like RMSE and MAE. It may provide a lot of help to financial analysts and investors in enhancing financial forecasting by integrating sentiment analysis with ML as per this study.

articleTitle: Improved Adaptive Fairness-Indexed Technique for Congestion Control in Underwater Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs), effective congestion control is essential for ensuring reliable data transmission and resource efficiency, especially in the face of challenging environmental factors such as water velocity, pressure, temperature, and salinity. This paper introduces a novel Adaptive Fairness-Indexed Congestion Control (AFICC) mechanism that employs Q-learning to dynamically adjust transmission rates among nodes, ensuring equitable resource distribution and minimizing congestion. Our simulations, conducted with 100 nodes at depths of up to 1000 meters, reveal that AFICC significantly outperforms two existing algorithms: Rate-Based Congestion Control (RBCC) and Energy-Aware Congestion Control (EACC). Specifically, AFICC achieved a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 93%, compared to 85% for RBCC and 80% for EACC. Additionally, the End-to-End Delay was reduced to an average of 150 milliseconds with AFICC, while RBCC and EACC recorded delays of 220 milliseconds and 210 milliseconds, respectively. AFICC also demonstrated a 25% improvement in Energy Efficiency over EACC and maintained a Jain’s Fairness Index of 0.92, surpassing the 0.82 and 0.78 indices achieved by RBCC and EACC, respectively. These results confirm that AFICC offers a robust framework for congestion control in UASNs, effectively adapting to fluctuating underwater conditions while ensuring reliable communication and equitable resource allocation.

articleTitle: Leveraging Large Language Models for Evaluating Customer Service Conversations and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Pre-Call Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Customer service is one of the critical aspects that determines the success of most businesses. Evaluating the conversational and performance efficiency of customer service representatives (CSRs) plays a huge role. However, conventional methods such as customer feedback and manual call reviews can be very time-consuming and inconsistent. This paper proposes the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to automate the evaluation of conversations that CSRs have with customers. By analyzing metrics such as empathy, tone, clarity, and problem resolution, LLMs objectively assess the CSR’s performance. This would help managers and CSRs with insights into conversational improvements, while RAG equips CSRs with relevant information before customer interactions. The results suggest that this approach not only automates efficiently the whole process of employee evaluation from the business’s perspective but also enhances the quality of customer interactions.

articleTitle: Application of Transformer-Based Language Models in Neuro-Linguistic Programming for Automated Personality Insights from Large-Scale Textual Corpora
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In the field of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), this study investigates the implementation of transformer-based language models to automate the extraction of personality insights from extensive textual corpora. With the use of transformer architectures such as GPT-3 and cutting-edge natural language processing methods, the work presents an innovative approach for identifying and analysing complex linguistic patterns present in large text corpora. In order to enable the models to capture subtle expressions associated with different aspects of personality, the process entails fine-tuning pre-trained transformer models on multiple datasets with annotated personality attributes. The primary goal is to create a reliable automated personality analysis system that can yield precise and comprehensive insights. Significant objectives include training and optimizing transformer models to enable personality trait prediction from textual input that has not been seen before. The GPT-3.5 transformer-based language model and the Hugging Face Transformers library were used to implement automated personality analysis. The model obtained an 85% accuracy, 86% precision, 84% recall, and 85% F1-score on the social media dataset. This research contributes to the growing field of personality analysis by combining NLP techniques with transformer-based language models, creating new opportunities for creative applications in the comprehension and interpretation of human conduct.

articleTitle: Exploring Nutraceuticals in Diabetes Mellitus Management through Machine Learning Techniques - A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: A chronic metabolic disorder called diabetes mellitus is characterized by elevated blood glucose levels. It results from deficiencies in insulin production, action, or both. Diabetes has traditionally been managed with insulin, oral hypoglycemic drugs, and lifestyle changes. However, growing interest in alternative medicine is often driven by conventional treatments' challenges and side effects. Nutraceuticals are becoming popular supplements for managing diabetic symptoms, as they are derived from food sources that provide health benefits beyond basic nutrition. This study explores the role of various nutraceuticals in preventing and managing diabetes mellitus, focusing on their mechanisms, effectiveness, and potential advantages. Additionally, the use of machine learning techniques to evaluate and predict the effectiveness of nutritional supplements in diabetes management is discussed.

articleTitle: Harnessing Medical Imaging Applications: Survey on 3D Deep Learning Models for Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The domain of 3D medical image segmentation has progressed markedly with the incorporation of deep learning methodologies, offering critical instruments for accurate and quick examination of intricate medical pictures. Various research has created 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) designed to segment diverse anatomical and pathological features, tackling specific issues such as high dimensionality, class imbalance, and computing requirements. Innovative models such as DeepMedic, which implemented a multiresolution strategy for brain lesion identification, together with other U-Net adaptations, have attained remarkable outcomes in tumor and organ segmentation through the integration of contextual and spatial data. Recent advancements encompass models employing large-kernel (LK) attention modules, transformer-based architectures, and hybrid approaches such as UNETR++ with Efficient Paired Attention, all enhancing accuracy while optimizing computing efficiency. These developments highlight the potential of 3D deep learning for clinical applications; yet, challenges such as restricted data availability, substantial annotation expenses, and generalizability across varied datasets persist as avenues for additional investigation.

articleTitle: An Robust Machine Learning Methods for Sentiments Analysis of Amazon Product in E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The rise in popularity of online platforms like social media, search engine optimisation, and email has propelled a field of Sentiment Analysis, which seeks to decipher an underlying meaning of a text, to the forefront of global discourse. In order to do sentiment analysis on Amazon product evaluations, this article presents a comparison examination of several machine learning algorithms. SVM, DT, RFC, CNN, and LSTM models will be the primary targets of their investigation. Research using sentiment analysis involves customers who are aware of how a product makes them feel. The data collection utilised is a Kaggle of product reviews from Amazon. It turns out that the LSTM ML algorithm is the most accurate of all the ones that were tried. The results show the LSTM model shows a higher accuracy of 97%, in comparison to other models. Research like this improves both the decision-making process and the online buying experience by shedding light on customer opinion.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Efficiency Through Machine Learning-Based Load Forecasting in power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Energy efficiency in buildings is critical for sustainable development. The design and expansion of power systems rely heavily on electrical demand forecasts. This study explores the use of LSTM models for enhancing energy load forecasting using a large dataset covering the period from September 2021 to August 2022. The methodology involves data preprocessing techniques such as normalisation, feature selection, and outlier removal to prepare the data for model training. The LSTM model is then applied to predict energy consumption, and its performance is evaluated using various metrics, including MSE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, RMSE, and MAE. The LSTM model achieves an MSE of 0.00295, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.86627, RMSE of 0.05436, and MAE of 0.04305, demonstrating high accuracy in predicting energy loads with minimal error. A comparative analysis with other models, such as GRU and CNN-ESN, shows that LSTM outperforms these models significantly, with lower MSE, RMSE, and MAE values. The study contributes to improved energy management and operational efficiency by providing a more reliable and precise forecasting model.

articleTitle: HFai: Deep Networks for Detecting Heart Failure Progression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Heart Failure affects millions worldwide, and early identification is crucial to prevent serious complications. Current diagnostic approaches depend mostly on human interpretation and are frequently inaccurate. Artificial Intelligence models are efficient for estimating heart failure progression since they provide healthcare professionals with more accurate and automated tools. This study aims to train and evaluate DL models (1D-CNN, DNN, ANN) on raw and feature-engineered cardiac arrest detection datasets. The performance of this model was first evaluated using heart disease data. On the raw dataset, ANN outperformed with the highest Accuracy of 80% and AUC of 82.74%. After feature engineering using XGBoost, ANN’s performance increased with an Accuracy of 95.08% and an AUC of 93.99%, indicating that feature engineering improves prediction. These findings emphasize the potential based on AI models in developing more reliable and automated diagnosis techniques for cardiac diseases. Future research will integrate real-time patient monitoring data with improved predictive models to detect developing health issues and allow for more accurate early diagnosis. This technique can transform heart failure therapy by providing personalized and more effective medicines, improving clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Device Authentication in IoT Security Application using Artificial Intelligence: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Technological advancement over the last decade has seen significant technological development, particularly in IoT, which is the most used and commercialized. This is due to its convenience, as it gives users remote control of their appliances via portable devices like smartphones and tablets, without needing to be physically present or close to those devices. As IoT technologies continue to grow and new innovative solutions for everyday applications are being developed there are more interconnected devices and large volumes of data being generated every second. However, the rapid growth of IoT has heightened security concerns, especially around device authentication. This paper reviews IoT authentication complexities and explores Machine Learning solutions under AI, comparing various algorithms and, providing a foundation for researchers and developers in the field.

articleTitle: EAMI: Efficient Privacy Preserving Authentication and Machine Learning Based Intrusion Detection in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) offer an effective communication platform between the vehicles and Road Side Units (RSUs), providing the backbone of intelligent transportation systems. However, ensuring secure communication in VANET is a major challenge due to the Open nature of wireless communication. Authentication plays a crucial role in VANET security, as it checks the authenticity of the users communicating in the network. This paper explores anonymous authentication with the support of Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) and bilinear pairing to allow only the authenticated entities to communicate in VANETs. Moreover, Support Vector Machine (SVM) based intrusion detection system is introduced in this paper to avoid unauthorized intrusion of malicious users. Further the performance of the proposed EAMI scheme is analyzed in terms of computational complexity with other existing authentication mechanisms to guarantee the efficiency of the proposed work. Through experimental analysis, the effectiveness of SVM based intrusion detection system is demonstrated in this paper to identify various types of intrusion, providing a robust solution to secure VANETs.

articleTitle: Performance optimization of Learning Trees modules in the ECL repository
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Multi-Node computation, also known as distributed computing, is a paradigm that allows for the efficient utilization of multiple interconnected nodes or machines to perform complex computational tasks. By dividing the workload and distributing it across multiple nodes, multi-node computation enables parallel processing, scalability, and improved performance for a wide range of applications. HPCC Systems® from LexisNexis Risk Solutions is a proven, open source solution for big data insights that can be implemented by businesses of all sizes. HPCC Systems offers a consistent data-centric programming language, two processing platforms and a single, complete end-to-end architecture for efficient processing. ECL is the Enterprise Control Language designed specifically for huge data projects using the HPCC Systems platform. It is extremely scalable and a powerful declarative data-processing language with native multi-processing capabilities and used for HPCC systems. Some core ECL functions, like the ones handling Learning Tree algorithms of Machine Learning Bundle are recursive in nature and hence high computational time is needed. This paper thus presents a solution to achieve optimized processing of ML learning tree algorithms in ECL through embedding python libraries. The proposed approach was tested on standard datasets and a significant decrease in computation time. For Real Estate Valuation Regression dataset the computation time was reduced from 11.371 seconds to 0.886 seconds using the proposed method showing 1324% improvement with no impact on the accuracy. Random Forests are also implemented using the proposed Decision Tree method allowing the users to specify the number of decision trees to be used in the forest.

articleTitle: Grad-CAM-Based Fine-Grained Classification for Celestial Object
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method of classifying celestial objects using Grad-Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) in conjunction with deep learning models such as VGG16, Google Net, Dense Net, and Efficient Net. The paper looks at the difficulties characterizing the enormous varieties of astronomical objects and the complexity that makes it difficult to classify the objects by conventional methods. From the empirical evaluation, it is clear that the Dense Net model has the ability to predict the right class of celestial objects with the help of Grad-CAM and has the highest accuracy of 99.76% for differentiating between images in the case of nebula. Grad-CAM works well at identifying the features that affect the model’s output. Thus, the integration of Grad-CAM with deep learning helps to increase the classification indicators and offers useful information regarding the morphological and spectral properties of the objects, thus, contributing to the further development of observational astronomy. It outperformed Class Activation Mapping (CAM) in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Quick Verification and Security Integrity of Emergency Messages Communication over Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Communication over wireless networks is increasingly vital for reliable, low-latency transmission of small messages by resource-constrained devices. These devices often struggle with the demands of implementing robust integrity security for emergency messages. Our solution, the BB-MAC (Bit by Bit Message Authentication Code) method, addresses this challenge with a quick, memory-efficient approach rooted in the Carter-Wegman structure. The key idea is to shift resource-intensive computations to idle periods, conserving critical time during latency-sensitive phases when new data must be processed. BB-MAC employs a universal hash function for Bit by Bit pre-computation of integrity security, minimizing XOR cycles during critical operations. Our research on embedded systems shows that BB-MAC outperforms recent methods in terms of delay and memory overhead, particularly for small payloads, making it a superior choice for safeguarding resource-limited devices under stringent security and latency requirements.

articleTitle: TherapAI: AI-Powered Therapy Chatbot with Sentiment Analysis, Mood Tracking, and Automated Reporting for Enhanced Mental Health Support
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The global mental health epidemic is creating an urgent need for easily accessible and efficient mental health care. We know that, often times even though it is helpful traditional therapy can be inadequate in terms of accessibility, affordability and scalability. In this paper, we present TherapAI, a therapy chatbot using AI to keep track of user mood through sentiment analysis; offering personalised emotional support 24/7 whilst generating activity summaries for therapists. Through the use of sophisticated Natural Language Processing (NLP), TherapAI tracks behavioral patterns and assists users in managing emotional stress, thereby promoting behavior change. It provides therapists with comprehensive information and allows for real-time emotional assistance through the analysis of user interactions.This could lead to positive testing, with customers having shown more effective emotional control and reporting themselves as satisfied after spending time interacting with the chatbot. According to therapists, those automated reports are a valuable addition and the mood tracking tool provides great data points. As a scalable AI solution, TherapAI can supplement traditional therapy and alleviate substantial gaps in the existing delivery of mental health care. It can also be upgraded to perhaps allow more words in the future.

articleTitle: Prescriptive Security Framework for Managing risks and Quantifying Security in Software Development Practices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Cyber-attacks are regular occurrence on software which can lead to serious consequences such as exposure of vulnerable system data. Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) strictly incorporates security specifically in final phase which makes the product vulnerable to security threats. The incorporation of security should be done from the initial phase of the SDLC but it is generally seen as an activity after development by most of the developers and companies. To address the security problems in SDLC multiple approaches are being developed which includes models, frameworks and methods. These approaches also improve the maturity and assurance level of the software. In this paper, we highlight various models for software development, and phases of development followed by SDLC. This paper also presents the security issues faced during the development of a software. It also analyses the frameworks, models and methods with SWOT parameters. Finally, we discuss the recent proposed ideas and changes about making a software secure.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning for Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a degenerative neurological condition that results in the deterioration of cognitive function. Early non-invasive detection is crucial for implementing timely interventions and slowing disease progression. In this research, we aimed to analyse the predictivity for classifying AD stages by integrating neuroimaging data—diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and structural MRI (sMRI)—with clinical biomarkers. In this paper Fractional Anisotropy (FA) scans, derived from DTI, denoting water molecule diffusion in brain tissue was assessed, particularly in identifying early microstructural changes during the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stage of AD. To progressively monitor the structural pathology of AD in patients, OASIS sMRI dataset was used. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) like ResNet 3D and LeNET were applied to analyse FA and sMRI data, achieving a significant accuracy score. In this proposed work, correlation and permutation analysis was also applied on the blood biomarker data to extract relevant features. Random Forest classifier was then used on these biomarkers. The highly correlated biomarkers were later used to obtain a significant impact in identifying the various stages of Alzheimer’s progression.

articleTitle: Automating Language Proficiency Evaluation in English Language Teaching: An NLP Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Language proficiency assessment is a critical aspect of English Language Teaching (ELT), serving as a foundation for gauging learners' language skills and guiding instructional strategies. However, traditional assessment methods often face challenges such as subjectivity, inefficiency, and potential biases, hindering accurate and objective evaluation. In response to these limitations, this study introduces a pioneering Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework aimed at transforming language proficiency assessment in ELT. The primary objective of this research is to develop an automated, objective, and scalable approach to language proficiency evaluation that aligns with established proficiency frameworks such as the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) or the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines. The novelty of the proposed framework lies in its innovative integration of advanced NLP techniques, particularly leveraging Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) models, with Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. The framework's architecture is designed to analyze linguistic data comprehensively, extracting relevant features and predicting proficiency levels accurately. Evaluation results showcase the framework's exceptional performance, achieving an accuracy of 98%, precision of 88%, recall of 82%, and F1-Score of 85%. These results underscore the framework's effectiveness in objectively assessing language proficiency levels across diverse educational settings. The contributions of this study extend beyond methodological advancements; they offer significant implications for practitioners and researchers in the field of ELT. The suggested framework has the potential to completely transform teaching and learning outcomes in ELT by offering a strong instrument for impartial and trustworthy language proficiency evaluation, promoting improved language acquisition and communication skills among students. This work represents a significant breakthrough in the field of language competency assessment, providing a game-changing approach to solve current issues and satisfy the changing requirements of language learners and educators in the digital era.

articleTitle: Reliability Enhancement of Multi-Cell Battery in Ground Control Station of Tethered HAPS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This paper investigates the reliability of a multi-cell battery system used in the Ground Control Station (GCS) of tethered High-Altitude Platform Systems (tHAPS), assuming the battery cells are series-connected. The model integrates repair and replenishment strategies to enhance battery reliability and ensure uninterrupted power supply to tHAPS. We analyze four practical variants, deriving explicit steady-state probabilities, which offer critical insights into system performance. Despite the inherent lower reliability of series-connected cells, our results demonstrate that effective management of repairs and replenishment significantly improves overall reliability. Additionally, the cost analysis indicates that increasing repair and replenishment rates reduces system costs by minimizing battery failures. The model underscores the importance of proper resource allocation and optimizing costs while maintaining high system reliability.

articleTitle: Efficient Mobile Edge Computing for Better Computation Offloading and Real Time Task Prediction Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Effective Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has become essential due to the quick spread of mobile devices and the rising demand for real-time applications. MEC lowers latency and improves performance by bringing processing resources closer to end users. In order to maximize computation offloading and real-time task prediction in MEC, this work explores the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods. We want to overcome the difficulties presented by dynamic and diverse network environments by utilizing DRL to increase the effectiveness of task execution and resource management. Significant gains in task prediction accuracy, offloading efficiency, and overall system performance are demonstrated by our suggested method. The dynamic and varied nature of mobile surroundings presents obstacles for MEC, despite its potential, in compute offloading and real-time task prediction. To maintain low latency, manage resource utilization, and balance the load between edge and cloud servers, effective offloading decisions are essential. Furthermore, proactive resource allocation and management depend on the ability to forecast real-time workloads with accuracy. In order to improve computation offloading and real-time task prediction, this research investigates the use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms in MEC. Our suggested architecture uses deep reinforcement learning to forecast activities in real time and make adaptive decisions on offloading, thus enhancing system performance.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Error Detection and Correction in English Writing Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: English writing tasks pose significant challenges for learners, especially when it comes to error detection and correction. In this research, we explore the potential of deep learning models to enhance error detection and correction mechanisms in English writing, aiming to improve both the accuracy and efficiency of these processes. Specifically, we employ a hybrid BERT-LSTM architecture, leveraging the language understanding capabilities of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and the sequential modelling strength of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. BERT, with its contextual embeddings, captures complex linguistic patterns, while LSTM processes these representations for improved prediction of grammatical, syntactical, and stylistic errors. The model is trained on large-scale datasets containing varied error types in English writing, enabling it to identify a broad spectrum of mistakes, including subject-verb agreement, article usage, punctuation, and contextual word choices. Our methodology incorporates transfer learning from BERT’s pre-trained model, fine-tuning it to the specific domain of error detection. The integration with LSTM allows the model to not only detect errors but also suggest contextually appropriate corrections, making it a comprehensive tool for writing improvement. Preliminary results show that the BERT-LSTM hybrid outperforms traditional grammar checkers and standalone models in terms of accuracy and error type coverage. The proposed system offers significant potential for applications in educational technologies, providing personalized feedback to language learners and aiding in the development of more proficient English writing skills. This research demonstrates the efficacy of advanced deep learning models in transforming English language writing tasks, offering insights for future improvements in natural language processing and educational tools.

articleTitle: HATO-Deep LSTM: Hybrid Adaptive Trust Aware Optimization Enabled Deep Learning Classifier For Energy Efficient Routing And Attack Mitigation In IoT-WSN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an emerging technology that gained significant attention in both academia as well as industry. It is a set of heterogeneous devices that are interconnected together for exchanging information between devices without any human intervention. Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) plays a major core part in IoT that enables to generation of seamless data and influences network lifespan. Each device in the WSN is referred to as a sensor node that can detect and process the sensor data between sensor nodes. Routing plays a major role in saving energy, but energy conservation is a major issue in resource-constrained networks. Hence, this research designs a Hybrid Adaptive Trust aware optimization based on Deep Long Short-Term Memory (HATO-Deep LSTM) for selecting the optimal node as cluster head (CH) and optimally performing the routing strategy. The trust factors determine the trustworthiness of all the adjoining nodes through collaboration among nodes and this factor enables the optimization to obtain the global best solution feasibly. The deep learning classifier employed in this research is highly effective in detecting malicious nodes by avoiding false nodes entering the data communication path. The proposed model effectively detects the misbehaving nodes and thereby the network throughput is increased. The performance attained by the proposed model in terms of number of alive nodes, end-to-end delay, throughput, and normalized energy is reported as 76, 0.81ms, 0.29bps, and 0.38J respectively with 100 number of nodes.

articleTitle: Leveraging Transformer-based LLMs to Understand Barriers and Enablers for Women in Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In recent years, transformer-based Language Models (TLMs), most notably known as Fine-tuned Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT), have emerged as potent research tools in the social sciences. This study explores the obstacles and facilitators that women in engineering education encounter using a Fine-tuned GPT. By means of a complete corpus analysis that includes academic literature, internet forums, and institutional records, the research endeavors to reveal subtle obstacles impeding women's involvement and accomplishment in engineering fields. The GPT is pre-trained on a large dataset of engineering education texts as part of the technique, and it is then particularly tuned to understand language related to gender. With this method, the model can identify underlying patterns that qualitative methods can miss and produce relevant responses.Important discoveries highlight structural problems that affect women's experiences in engineering education, including widespread gender stereotypes, implicit biases, and a lack of mentorship opportunities. The study also finds important facilitators that help women's academic and professional success in engineering areas, such as encouraging learning environments, positive role models, and inclusive legislation. GPT research provides insights that can be used by educational institutions and policymakers to develop focused actions that promote gender equity in engineering education. This study adds to the growing body of research on using natural language processing methods to address societal issues, especially those pertaining to gender diversity in STEM professions. The model's ability to handle bigger and more varied datasets will be improved in the future, along with the exploration of new intersectionality dimensions and the long-term effects of interventions meant to improve inclusion in engineering education.

articleTitle: Explainable Test Case Prioritization in Continuous Integration through Incremental Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In Continuous Integration (CI) environments, where software undergoes frequent updates, regression testing is vital in ensuring software quality. However, rerunning every test case becomes impractical with the constant changes. Test Case Prioritization (TCP) addresses this issue, and Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly used to manage regression testing. However, many ML models struggle to adapt to new features or changes in CI and lack transparency, complicating the regression process. To address these issues, we propose an incremental learning-based explainable ML model for TCP in CI environments, which adaptively incorporates new changes. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to evaluate feature contributions and help testers understand the model's functionality. Our model is trained and tested on 20 open-source software projects. Its performance is assessed using Accuracy and F1 Score, while test case prioritization is evaluated with the Average Percentage of Faults Detected (APFD) and a new metric, the Failed Test Ranking Score (FTRS).

articleTitle: Leveraging Swin Transformer for Robust Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The massive deployment of deepfake technology has underlined the critical urgency of appropriate detection mechanisms to mitigate its potential harms. Proper motivation emanates from the perceived increasing threat of misinformation dissemination, accompanied by the harmful impacts of its content on society. Based on the Swin Transformer model, this work presented a deepfake detection solution for addressing the challenge of achieving detection accuracy and being resilient to new sophisticated manipulation techniques. The research problem revolves around the existing inadequacy in the available detection techniques and how to fight against the rapid evolution of deepfake techniques. Our model was trained using LCC-FASD and CASIA datasets combined, which provide large data of real and fake images from various resources. When training the model, several batches of training samples are fed to the system and processed over several epochs depending on each class of the samples to improve the accuracy of the classification that is performed using the Label Smoothing Cross entropy Loss Function. The model undergoes great pre-processing and a high level of training to effectively differentiate between real and fake content. The results are promising, with an overall accuracy of 95.4%, while it was approximately 81% for real images and 94.1% for fake ones. These findings underline the robustness of the Swin Transformer model in reliably detecting deep-fakes, adding confidence and integrity in digital media to counteract adverse effects due to synthetic media manipulations.

articleTitle: A New Federated Learning Framework for Plant Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Several Deep Learning-based approaches have recently been proposed for plant leaf disease detection. Traditional learning-based models necessitate centralizing large image datasets, requiring huge volumes of storage space. It appears that a better predictive model can be developed if the available data at multiple data sites can be effectively utilized using a collaborative learning strategy. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized alternative, enabling collaborative model training by allowing multiple participants to update a global model using their local data without sharing high volumes of raw image datasets. Our work presents an FL framework to train a Vision Transformer-based model with an improved Federated Averaging (FedLossAvg) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate our model’s capability to handle large, varied datasets. Using four clients, our global model achieved an F1-score of 95.62% and an accuracy of 99.89% on the PlantVillage data.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fraud Detection Techniques in Credit Card and Internet Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In an era where financial services are easily accessible, financial fraud has emerged as a widespread threat, aimed at unlawfully seizing assets from individuals, businesses, and institutions. Crimes like credit card and internet banking fraud present serious risks to the financial ecosystem. Criminals exploit card information using techniques such as identity theft, skimming, and phishing, causing substantial economic losses each year. Similarly, the rise of internet banking fraud, where unauthorized access to accounts often results from weaknesses in authentication systems, has further disrupted the financial sector. Detecting such fraudulent activities is especially difficult due to the ever-changing tactics of perpetrators, the large volume of transaction data, and technical challenges like data imbalance and concept drift. This paper examines the landscape of financial fraud, with a specific emphasis on credit card and internet banking fraud. It begins by providing an overview of the issue and its impact on the modern economic environment, followed by an exploration of various fraud detection methods. Additionally, the paper addresses key challenges in fraud detection and highlights the need for innovative approaches to effectively combat the growing threat of financial crime.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Faults in High Voltage Transmission Lines Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: There is a possibility that errors in the transmission line will be difficult to identify and categorize. Since the beginning of time, this issue has been present. This was one of the most difficult obstacles that the power had to face. For the most part, the protective relay device, tape, and management and security software systems are utilized for the purpose of detecting the problem and disconnecting the damaged unit of the system from the other units. The identification and classification of flaws is the primary subject of this paper, when it comes to transmission cables that support high voltage the detection of faults is also included. The categorizing process involves the utilization of artificial neural networks (ANN). The back-propagation algorithm makes use of a network of computers in order to direct the distribution for each of the three steps that comprise the fault process. The process of identifying and classifying research into neural networks by employing many buried layers of neurons, each of which had a unique sum, was subject to the necessity that the choice of neural network at each step be made. Using this concept as the foundation for a conventional transmission, the creation of a line for producing the voltage and current settings was carried out. MATLAB/SIMULINK network is used whose simplification was selected as the choice Carry out simulations of every feasible scenario involving the development of defects and tests. Using recently developed test data sets, the Ann is trained and then put through a series of tests to identify any errors. Mistakes in classification and detection occurred. The results of the simulation demonstrated that such models, which are based on artificial neural networks, can achieve performance fulfillment. These models are designed to facilitate the efficient organization and identification of defects on transmission lines.

articleTitle: Investigate the Impact of Path-loss on Channel Capacity in IRS-Assist Dual-hop Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) is an emerging and expanding technology that will develop an intelligent radio environment for next-generation wireless standards. In this paper, we explore our vision to design an IRS-assist wireless communication system for uninterrupted connectivity between transceiver terminals, along with measuring the impact of path loss on the average capacity (bits/sec/Hz) of the system indicates the novelty of the works. Four different schemes such as optimal rate adaption (ORA), side information at the transmitter and the receiver (OPRA), channel inversion with fixed rate (CIFR), and truncated channel inversion with fixed rate (TIFR) have been considered to examine the effect of path loss on the average capacity of the system. This investigation ensure higher order of reflecting elements and quantization level can mitigate the effect of path loss in the system. In addition, numerical simulation results from MATLAB have been provided to validate the analytical results.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient RF Harvesting System for Self-Sustaining Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Advancements in low-power CMOS technology have enabled innovative circuit designs for sensor systems, including implantable and wearable devices, as well as wireless sensor nodes (WSNs). However, the challenge of powering these systems persists due to the slower progress in battery technology, which limits the integration of multiple sensor modules and poses risks such as leakage in medical implants. Energy harvesting has emerged as a promising alternative, utilizing ambient sources like RF signals, wind, solar, mechanical vibrations, and thermal energy to power these devices. This study focuses on RF and piezoelectric vibration-based energy scavenging systems, particularly using MOSFETs in novel circuit designs to harness RF energy. Implemented in a 130 nm CMOS process, these designs demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of RF energy harvesting in creating self-sustaining, energy-efficient sensor systems. The findings contribute significantly to the development of more functional and safer sensor applications across various fields.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Dynamic and Energy-Efficient Workload Migration in Cloud Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Resource allocation and energy efficiency optimization have become increasingly crucial needs in the fast-evolving landscape of cloud computing, driven by increasing user demands and shrinking environmental windows. The paper introduces a Hybrid Deep Learning Framework that operates with Dynamic and Energy-Efficient Workload Migration. Using the combination of both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM), the workload management can be improved in the cloud environment to a very great extent. With real-time data from a cloud workload, the use of the proposed framework focuses on Min-Max normalization during pre-processing, which adapts uniform scaling of the features given: CPU usage, memory utilization, and energy consumption. This preprocessing stage enables the CNN to effectively derive meaningful patterns and characteristics of resource demands and energy trends. The complex sequences are learned in the LSTM network that is used for predicting future workload behaviors based on temporal dependencies in the data. With this impressive accuracy of 98%, the hybrid approach widely outperforms existing methodologies including standalone CNN and LSTM models, which thereby proves its effectiveness in the predictions of workload shifts and optimization of energy usage. The implementation of the framework in Python further enhances the performance of prediction besides providing a feedback loop mechanism for refining adaptation of the model based on evaluation metrics. This iterative improvement process allows the framework to evolve and respond to changed dynamics in workloads, thereby contributing to more sustainable and efficient cloud computing infrastructures. With a focus on both operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, this hybrid deep learning framework, it demonstrates an attractive solution towards the challenges of modern cloud resource management problems.

articleTitle: Optimized Virtual Machine Scheduling for Green Cloud Computing Using MLP-LSTM with Sheep Flock Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: With the growing demand for cloud computing services, it is important to efficiently manage resources using proper strategies in order to save energy consumption while retaining high-level performance. The innovative framework proposed here utilizes the MLP and LSTM models with a bio-inspired optimization algorithm in order to improve workload predictions and resource allocation for Virtual Machine (VM) scheduling. This work has an effective framework for energy-aware virtual machine scheduling in cloud computing environments using MLP-LSTM hybrid models optimized by the Sheep Flock Optimization algorithm, and comprehensive datasets it uses involve essential workload features, such as CPU and memory utilization. The proposed methodology utilizes the min-max normalization during data preprocessing, which ensures uniform scaling of all features. In the integrated MLP-LSTM model, an impressive accuracy of 98.7% was obtained for the task of prediction. Moreover, it was even better than other existing methodologies including Random Forest and Decision Tree. Using the predictions from the MLP-LSTM model, the SFO algorithm optimizes VM placement and migration, reduces energy consumption by a large margin, but at the same time maintains balanced resource distribution across all the physical servers. The results demonstrate the enhancement of both operational efficiency and energy usage, hence the sustainability of cloud computing. The implementation of the framework in Python gives it a realistic solution to situations that pose challenges to resource management in modern cloud infrastructures. This research validates the potential use of an advanced ML approach in conjunction with optimization techniques that can succeed in creating a green and efficient overall ecosystem for cloud computing.

articleTitle: Predicting Road Accident Severity and Identifying High-Risk Areas Using Tree-based Learning: A Case Study from the UK
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Road accidents are a pressing global issue, often resulting in injuries ranging from minor to fatal. This study leverages machine learning algorithms to predict the severity and location of road accidents, with the aim of enhancing road safety measures. Utilizing accident data from the UK, we developed predictive models that classify the severity of accidents on a scale from 1 to 5, where 1 represents the least severe and 5 represents the most severe outcomes. The model’s predictions have been integrated into a user-friendly application, providing visual insights into accident severity and highlighting high-risk areas on a map. By identifying and visualizing accident-prone locations, this study offers a valuable tool for authorities to implement targeted interventions, potentially reducing the frequency and impact of road accidents. The findings underscore the potential of machine learning in proactive road safety management, contributing to efforts that could save lives and minimize the societal costs associated with road accidents.

articleTitle: Impact of Social Media On Mental Health
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: This research examines the influence of social media on mental health, particularly highlighting significant instances of students exhibiting high rates of melancholy and anxiety. This research examines the good and negative effects of social media, particularly among teens, in a comprehensive analysis. Social media facilitated social engagement, enhanced communication, and disseminated information. Nonetheless, it remains a significant concern since it facilitates cyberbullying, diminishes self-esteem, and exacerbates mental health issues. The study employed a descriptive research methodology, utilizing data collected from surveys and secondary sources. Additional methodologies employed included statistical analyses such as Crosstabs, ANOVA, and correlation analysis to identify trends and interrelationships between social media usage and mental health issues. This study elucidates the bimodal character of social media, highlighting its function in fostering relationships as well as its association with adverse psychological effects. This necessitates a heightened awareness of the many degrees and patterns of social media activity that influence students' mental health, specifically concerning anxiety and depression. Conclusion This study advocates for heightened awareness and the implementation of intervention measures to alleviate the adverse effects of social media, ensuring that this activity enhances rather than undermines mental well-being.

articleTitle: Optimized Hybrid CNN-GRU Approach for Accurate Prediction of Cardiovascular Diseases: Integrating Medical Imaging and Clinical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: As the primary cause of death globally, cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) demand precise and timely prediction to enhance patient outcomes. Other examples of conventional approaches for CVD prediction include statistical models as well as machine learning models such as a single model that often struggle to address complex and comprehensive data from clinical records and Medical Imaging. To address these issues, the concept proposed here is to integrate the medical imaging data with clinical data as new apart from utilizing the hybrid CNN–GRU model to predict cardiovascular diseases with higher accuracy and interpretability. While the GRU module deals with the time sequences of clinical data including past history and other test results, the CNN module is to extract the spatial features from the medical images. Thus, by integrating these modules, it is more accurate to predict the data of the patient as a synergy of spatial and temporal arrangements. Cross-validation techniques and performance indices are used for model training and testing on a diverse data set containing imaging and other clinical-related data. Experimental results depict that the suggested hybrid CNN-GRU model performs much better than the traditional approaches and has higher levels of predicted accuracy and robustness. It is also feasible to generalize this integrated strategy to other medical disorder where multi-modal data analysis is crucial, besides enhancing the capacity to estimate CVDs. The findings underline the importance of integrating doctors’ information with radiological images and applying new patterns of neural networks to augmenting clinical judgment. The suggested work is implemented using python.

articleTitle: Predictive Feedback Loops: Harnessing AI for Continuous Assessment and Personalized Growth in English Language Learners
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: English language learning involves acquiring the ability to understand, speak, read, and write in English. It focuses on developing skills in vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and comprehension, often through structured lessons and practice. English proficiency is essential for communication in global settings, education, and professional environments. This research explores the application of predictive feedback loops, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) to revolutionize continuous assessment and personalized growth in English language learners. By employing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, the study aims to provide a dynamic framework that monitors and evaluates student progress over time, enabling educators to deliver personalized feedback tailored to individual learning needs. LSTM, known for its ability to process and predict time series data, is uniquely suited for tracking linguistic progress, capturing both short-term achievements and long-term language acquisition patterns. The proposed model continuously analyzes learners' performance in various language tasks, identifying gaps in comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, and fluency. Through real-time assessments, the system offers immediate and actionable feedback, creating a loop of evaluation, adjustment, and improvement. This feedback loop fosters adaptive learning environments, where instruction is tailored to the learner's evolving needs, promoting more efficient language development. The research investigates the model's efficacy in enhancing language proficiency, focusing on its role in improving self-regulation, motivation, and learner autonomy. By providing timely, personalized interventions, the LSTM-based framework supports continuous learner growth, helping educators move beyond traditional, static assessment methods. Ultimately, this AI-driven approach aims to optimize the language learning experience, ensuring sustained progress and meaningful engagement in English language acquisition.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of free space optical communication system in the presence of hardware and misalignment impairments using aperture averaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Significant growth has been seen in expanding the worldwide optical communication system in free space (FSO). But despite the many benefits that FSO communication offers, there are several problems with how optical networks are designed. Aperture averaging is one of the most often used strategies for overcoming issues, including scattering, diffraction, turbulence, and other issues. The primary goal of this research is on aperture averaging, and bit error rate (BER) attainable objectives have been analyzed using Opti system software for a range of receiver data rates and aperture diameters.

articleTitle: A Study of the Security and Privacy Risks in Health-Related Mobile Applications in India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: With the increased adoption of mobile devices in the current scenario, the number of applications in every category has also skyrocketed. In recent years, health-related applications have also become increasingly common. This paper aims to investigate whether the increasing prevalence of health-related applications has been accompanied by the implementation of robust cyber-security and privacy measures. In our analysis of the 21 most popular health-related Android applications available on the Google Play Store in India, it has been observed that 95% of the applications have the M8: Security Misconfiguration vulnerability of the OWASP Mobile Top 10 – 2024. It was also found that 90% of the applications have embedded trackers, which can have tremendous privacy and security implications, given the sensitive nature of health-related information. These trackers may collect sensitive user information, often without user consent and may introduce additional vulnerabilities into the application. These findings underscore the need for the adoption of security best practices in the development of health-related applications. It also shows the need for effective implementation of security and privacy regulations such as the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India) 2023.

articleTitle: Adaptive Testing with Machine Learning: Customizing English Proficiency Assessments Based on Learner Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The implementation of adaptive testing for English proficiency assessments using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to customize evaluations based on learner performance. The dataset utilized is Classification of English Learner Proficiency, consists of essays ranging from 20 to 300 words, categorized into six Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) levels: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, and C2. The research emphasizes a thorough data preprocessing phase, which includes text cleaning and normalization to enhance data quality, followed by feature extraction and tokenization to prepare the textual data for analysis. The core of the study presents a proposed adaptive testing method that leverages a DRL agent to optimize question selection, adjusting the difficulty based on real-time learner performance metrics such as accuracy and response time. This adaptive approach not only personalizes the assessment experience but also maintains learner engagement by presenting appropriately challenging content. The evaluation of the proposed system involves comparative studies against traditional testing methods to assess improvements in learner outcomes and satisfaction. Initial findings indicate that the DRL-driven adaptive testing framework significantly enhances the accuracy of proficiency level predictions while reducing assessment time. Key evaluation metrics demonstrate strong performance, with a precision of 0.92, recall of 0.95, an F1-score of 0.90, and overall accuracy reaching 96%. This research highlights the potential of integrating advanced machine learning techniques in language education, paving the way for more responsive and individualized assessment methodologies.

articleTitle: Feature Selection using Modified PSO with Mutual Information for Tomato Leaf Disease Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Automated disease detection in agriculture is one of the primary focus areas of researchers recently. The captured images are used as input to diagnose the diseases in plants. However, during automated diagnosis, the large number of features with respect to each image is one of the major challenges. The optimal feature selection techniques applied to these input images are often stuck into the local optimum. These features often share a large amount of mutual information, which can be used to reduce the dimensionality of feature set at the primary level before applying any standard feature selection approach.
