In this work, we have exploited the mutual information to reduce the size of feature set and then applied one of the most popular optimization techniques, PSO, to obtain the optimal feature set. We have compared the results with the optimal features in the absence of any prior reduction in the dimensionality of the feature set.

articleTitle: Edge-Cloud based Framework to Offload Task in Vehicular Edge Computing Using Optimized Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) is rapidly gaining traction to satisfy computationally demanding vehicular applications such as autonomous driving, monitoring traffic flow, remote vehicle diagnostics, and vehicular online gaming. Nevertheless, many existing offloading schemes fail to consider the edge computing environment’s fluctuating nature, leading to increased delays and high energy consumption. This paper introduces an optimized edge-cloud based task offloading scheme utilizing deep reinforcement learning for VEC networks. Depending on the specific computation and memory needs, this system enables tasks requiring a lot of computing to be managed locally or delegated to a cloud or edge server. By simultaneously considering i) the dynamic nature of the vehicular edge computing network and ii) the necessity for swift offloading decisions, our approach leverages deep reinforcement learning to reduce energy usage and the average processing delay of tasks through seamless integration of the cloud, edge servers, and vehicular computing resources.

articleTitle: Unveiling Market Anomalies: Harnessing Convolutional Neural Networks for Fraud Detection in Finance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The process of financial fraud detection is essential for the sound functioning of financial markets. Conventional techniques cannot detect more complex forms of fraud, as such advanced techniques are necessary. This research aims to explore a new technique based on CNNs with attention mechanisms for improved fraud-detecting techniques. Transaction data from Kaggle which contain a diverse range of purchases and market trends were gathered and scaled through Min-Max normalization. The attention mechanism was used for feature selection and control over noise at the same time, focusing on important features. The developed CNN model has trained to identify the higher order feature of data and it shows a prominent performance of detecting the fraudulent activities. The proposed model has high accuracy of 99.12% which surpass traditional techniques and basic models like TransUNet, MedT, and FAT-Net by 19.36%. Systematic performance appraisal with proven examples as to how it may be applied served as the basis for this study. Based on the results of the current paper, the efficiency of CNNs in detecting market irregularities, and the importance of deep learning methods in fraud detection in finance are highlighted. This research was developed in Python to strengthen the security of financial systems, and ultimately promoting more trust and accuracy to the markets of finance across the globe.

articleTitle: Optimizing Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Based on Machine Learning-Based Churn Prediction Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: In this era of changing marketplaces and intense rivalry among companies, customer relationship management (CRM) and data-driven marketing have become critical. Retaining current clients is one of the most crucial aspects of CRM. In order to forecast customer churn, this research makes use of ML algorithms. A classifier-based model for churn prediction using customer data is presented in this study. These trials make use of four different ML classifiers. The first step is to forecast the customer's churn status using these ML classifiers. Use the ADASYN to zero in on the problems with unbalanced datasets. This is to ascertain an efficacy of the model by measuring its F1-score, precision, recall, and accuracy. XGBoost outperforms all other models with the highest accuracy (96.71%), precision (87.60%), recall (92.62%), and F1-score (90.04%), demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting customer churn. While RF also performs well, CNN struggles to match traditional models, and LR shows a trade-off between recall and precision. The work adds to the body of literature on churn prediction by highlighting the integration of DL with conventional ML techniques and proving the better performance of XGBoost.

articleTitle: Multi-Relationship Features based Residual Network for Fake Review Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: The proliferation of e-commerce platforms has significantly affected user experience due to the advent of fake reviews. To circumvent platform detection, fake reviews have become increasingly challenging to identify. Contemporary approaches for detecting fraudulent reviews utilising Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) frequently experience network degradation and gradient vanishing problems during extensive training. Furthermore, it examines the impact of camouflage outcomes on the skewed tagging of reviews, which undermines the robustness of GNN detection models. Multi-relationship review detection on residual networks (MRDRN) is presented to combine multi-relational review elements to identify fraudulent reviews. Initially, the approach employs a residual network for comprehensive feature extraction to alleviate network degradation. It proposes an innovative neighbour-mixing sampling strategy, which conducts low-order and high-order neighbour-mixing sampling predicated on feature similarity among reviewers. This mitigates the issue of uneven review labelling and facilitates the acquisition of more nuanced review characteristics. Secondly, a multi-relational review feature fusion technique is developed, which mitigates the effects of review camouflage by incorporating the network architecture of reviews inside a relation and the comprehensive fusing of multi-relational review features. Experiments performed on three real-world datasets indicate that MRDRN exhibits superior detection capabilities and enhanced robustness relative to baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Improving Text Summarization with Transformer Networks and Reinforcement Learning for English
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Control, and Intelligent Systems (CCIS)
abstract: As the volume of text data continues to grow rapidly, efficient and accurate text summarization has become crucial for managing and processing this information. Traditional summarization methods, including extractive and abstractive approaches, face challenges in maintaining relevance, fluency, and factual consistency, particularly in complex domains such as legal documents. In this research, we propose an advanced summarization framework leveraging transformer networks, specifically designed to enhance the quality of English text summaries. The framework begins with the preprocessing of text data, including lowercasing, elimination of punctuation, HTML tags, stopwords, and stemming/lemmatization to standardize the input. Text feature extraction is then performed using the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) method, converting textual data into numerical representations that highlight the significance of terms within documents. The core of the framework employs a transformer model that eschews traditional RNNs in favor of multiple attention layers and positional encoding to capture global dependencies and enable parallel processing. The model's encoder-decoder structure uses self-attention mechanisms and multi-head attention layers to effectively encode the sequence and context of words, leading to high-quality abstractive summaries. The proposed architecture's effectiveness is evaluated using the BillSum dataset, which includes over 22,000 U.S. Congressional bills and human-written summaries. The results highlight the superior performance of the proposed Transformer model, which achieved the highest ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L scores, with values of 37.03, 16.89, and 28.34, respectively and the Proposed method is implemented using python software. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements in summary accuracy and relevance compared to existing methods, making it a promising solution for automated summarization tasks across various domains.
